summary: Blueprint of the new roadmap ScholzeFunctorAndModpCohomologyOfTheLubinTateTower at target level: 29 nodes in seven layers, built from Colmez–Dospinescu–Nizioł (Forum Math. Pi 2023) §§3–4 and the papers they use in full (Scholze 2018, Ludwig 2017, Fust 2022, Paškūnas 2022, Dospinescu–Paškūnas–Schraen 2023, Gee–Kisin 2014 Appendix A, Strauch 2008, Moore 1968). SZ.0 sets up equivariant étale sites, the Gross–Hopkins period map as a pro-étale GLₙ(F)-torsor, Strauch’s connected components and finiteness for admissible representations of compact p-adic Lie groups. SZ.1 constructs Scholze’s sheaf ℱ_π and the functors Sⁱ, and proves Scholze’s finiteness theorem (with the strict-image and Frobenius almost-module lemmas) with the Galois action, S⁰, central characters and twists. SZ.2 plans Fust’s continuous cohomology of p-adic groups, Moore’s vanishing of H² of SL₂(ℚ_p) mod p, the Cartan–Leray spectral sequence Hⁱ(G, H^j(M_∞, π)) ⇒ S^{i+j}(π) and the comparison map for S¹. SZ.3 plans Ludwig’s perfectoid Borel quotient and the vanishing of S² on principal series and Steinberg twists. SZ.4 globalises a residual representation, controls the definite quaternionic block module and Paškūnas’s torsion comparison, and proves the key local proposition on Galois invariants of S¹(I(χ₁, χ₂)). SZ.5 proves that the functor of multiplicities has finite image and the finite-length theorem for H¹_ét(M^p_{n,K}, k_L)^∨. SZ.6 proves finiteness of multiplicities for every F, finite length and vanishing of the geometric multiplicities Π^geo_n(ρ̄), and the finiteness of Lubin–Tate smooth vectors. One gap remains: CDN Theorem 2.1, owned by the pending pro-étale cohomology design. Six source issues are independently checked: Fust’s version-dependent lemma number, the prime-to-p limitation of the cited projection-formula proof, the height-two scalar quotient, the degree-zero reduced-norm convention conflict, the missing dual in CDN Corollary 2.12, and the coefficient-dual slip already corrected in DPS23. The plan uses the DPS common-central-character convention.

nodes.title: Equivariant étale sites of continuous actions and of towers
nodes.statement: Let G be a locally profinite group acting continuously on X, a locally noetherian analytic adic space or a perfectoid space (X is covered by affinoids Spa(A, A⁺) whose stabiliser H ⊂ G is open and acts continuously on A), and let (X/G)_ét be the equivariant étale site: objects are adic spaces Y with a continuous G-action and a G-equivariant étale map Y → X, covers are jointly surjective families. Then: (a) (limit formula) if X is qcqs and G is profinite, for every closed subgroup H₀ ⊂ G the topos of (X/H₀)_ét is the projective limit of the topoi of (X/H)_ét over the open subgroups H ⊃ H₀, so H^i((X/H₀)_ét, ℱ) = colim_{H ⊃ H₀ open} H^i((X/H)_ét, ℱ) for every sheaf ℱ on (X/G)_ét; for H₀ = 1 this computes H^i(X_ét, ℱ). (b) (slices) for H ⊂ G open, U ↦ U ×^H G identifies (X/H)_ét with the slice of (X/G)_ét over X ×^H G. (c) (conservativity and O⁺/ϖ) a pointed sheaf on (X/G)_ét is trivial iff its pullback to X_ét is trivial; if X lies over Spa(K, O_K) with pseudo-uniformiser ϖ, U ↦ ((O⁺_X/ϖ)(U))^G is a sheaf O⁺_{X/G}/ϖ on (X/G)_ét whose pullback to X_ét is O⁺_X/ϖ. (d) (towers) if G is profinite, (X_H)_H → X is a G-torsor tower (each X_H → X a finite étale G/H-torsor for H ⊴ G open, compatibly), X_∞ is a perfectoid space with X_∞ ∼ lim_H X_H, and a locally profinite group J acts continuously on X and on every X_H commuting with G, then pullback (X/J)_ét → (X_∞/G × J)_ét is an equivalence of sites, and for J trivial O⁺_X/p corresponds to O⁺_{X_∞/G}/p under (X_∞/G)_ét ≃ X_ét. (e) (Hochschild–Serre) if X is qcqs and K is a profinite group acting continuously, for every sheaf 𝒢 of abelian groups on (X/K)_ét there is a spectral sequence E₂^{ij} = H^i_cont(K, H^j(X_ét, 𝒢)) ⇒ H^{i+j}((X/K)_ét, 𝒢), with the K-modules H^j(X_ét, 𝒢) smooth (discrete).
hypotheses: G locally profinite and the action continuous in the sense of Scholze’s Definition 2.1; X locally noetherian analytic (locally Spa of a strongly noetherian Tate ring) or perfectoid.

In (a) and (e) X is qcqs and the group profinite; in (d) X is a locally noetherian analytic adic space over Spa(ℚ_p, ℤ_p) (not perfectoid), G is profinite, J locally profinite, and X_∞ ∼ lim X_H in the sense of Scholze–Weinstein Definition 2.4.1; the O⁺/p correspondence in (d) is asserted for J trivial, as in the source.

Scholze spells out the locally noetherian case and notes that perfectoid X works the same way; he states (e) for ℙ^{n−1}_C, and the proof applies verbatim to any qcqs X, smoothness of the K-modules coming from (a).
proofSteps: (a) Show that qcqs objects of (X/H₀)_ét form the 2-colimit of the qcqs objects of (X/H)_ét over open H ⊃ H₀: rational subsets have open stabilisers (Scholze Lemma 2.2), and actions on finite étale covers spread out from H₀ to an open H by the approximation theorem for finite étale algebras over completed filtered colimits of complete Tate rings (Elkik–Gabber–Ramero; Scholze Theorem 2.4 and Lemma 2.3, Corollary 2.5); then apply the limit theorem for fibred coherent topoi (SGA 4 VI 8.2.3) to get the topos and the cohomology colimit.
(b) The inverse functor sends a G-equivariant U → X ×^H G to its fibre over X = X ×^H H; covers correspond.

(c) Conservativity: a section trivial on X_ét is trivial on (X/H)_ét for some open H by (a), and U ×^H G → U is a cover. The O⁺/ϖ sheaf: take G-invariants in the sheaf property; by continuity of the action every section over a qcqs U is invariant under an open subgroup, which gives the pullback by (a).

(d) Reduce to J compact and X, X_H, X_∞ qcqs; quasi-compact opens descend because |X_∞| = lim |X_H|, and finite étale covers descend by the approximation theorem again; finite étale descent along X_H → X gives the equivalence. For O⁺/p compute the pullback along (X_∞)_ét → X_ét with Scholze’s comparison for tilde-limits (perfectoid P5/P7) and check it on X_∞ by (c).
IgusaVarieties IG.4 supplies only the site (X/G)_ét with its pullback and slice functors; statements (a)–(e) are proved here.

(e) For K′ ⊴ K open, X ×^{K′} K → X is a cover in (X/K)_ét whose Čech nerve is X × (K/K′)^•, giving a Cartan–Leray spectral sequence H^{i}(K/K′, H^j((X/K′)_ét, 𝒢)) ⇒ H^{i+j}((X/K)_ét, 𝒢); pass to the colimit over K′ using (a), which turns the colimit of finite-group cohomology into continuous cohomology of K with discrete coefficients (ProfiniteCohomology).
acceptance: For G trivial (X/G)_ét is X_ét and (e) degenerates to H^j(X_ét, 𝒢).

For K finite acting trivially on a qcqs X and with trivial K-linearisation on 𝒢, (e) is the group-cohomology spectral sequence for the trivial action on RΓ(X_ét, 𝒢). An arbitrary equivariant sheaf can carry a non-trivial K-action even when the action on X is trivial.

For a compact open K ⊂ GLₙ(F), the Lubin–Tate K-tower gives (M_{LT,K}/D^×)_ét ≃ (M_{LT,∞}/(K × D^×))_ét. The base of this compact-group descent is M_{LT,K}; descent from the full GLₙ(F)-torsor to projective space is a separate step of SZ.0/gross-hopkins-torsor and SZ.1/scholze-sheaf.

nodes.title: The Gross–Hopkins period map as a pro-étale GLₙ(F)-torsor
nodes.statement: Let F/ℚ_p be finite, n ≥ 1, D the central division algebra over F of invariant 1/n, G = GLₙ(F), and (M_{LT,K})_K the Lubin–Tate tower over F̆ (all quasi-isogeny heights), indexed by the compact open subgroups K ⊂ G, with D^× acting on each level, G acting on the tower (g : M_{LT,K} ≅ M_{LT,g⁻¹Kg}) and Weil descent data; for a compact open K not of the form 1 + ϖ^m Mₙ(O_F), M_{LT,K} is the quotient of M_{LT,K_m} (K_m ⊂ K normal) by the free action of the finite group K/K_m. (a) The Gross–Hopkins period maps π_GH : M_{LT,K} → ℙ^{n−1}_{F̆} are compatible in K, étale and surjective, with fibres GLₙ(F)/K over every geometric point; they are D^×-equivariant when ℙ^{n−1}_{F̆} is identified with the Brauer–Severi variety of D (split over F̆), and compatible with the Weil descent data. (b) For K′ ⊂ K compact open with K′ normal in K, M_{LT,K′} → M_{LT,K} is a finite étale K/K′-torsor; the infinite level M_{LT,∞} ∼ lim_K M_{LT,K} (perfectoid after base change to a complete algebraically closed C) therefore makes M_{LT,∞} → M_{LT,K} a profinite K-torsor tower in the sense of SZ.0/equivariant-site-toolkit (d), for every K. (c) After base change to C = ℂ_p (or any complete algebraically closed C/F̆), write M_∞ = M_{LT,∞,C}; there is an isomorphism of diamonds over ℙ^{n−1}_C, M_∞ × G → M_∞ ×_{ℙ^{n−1}_C} M_∞, (x, g) ↦ (x, x·g), and more generally the (k+1)-fold fibre product of M_∞ over ℙ^{n−1}_C is M_∞ × G^k; thus π_GH : M_∞ → ℙ^{n−1}_C is a pro-étale G-torsor whose Čech nerve is M_∞ × G^•.
hypotheses: n ≥ 1, F/ℚ_p finite; G is viewed as a locally profinite set, so M_∞ × G is the disjoint union over the compact open cosets.

The torsor statement (c) is a statement about diamonds (or about the equivariant site of SZ.0/equivariant-site-toolkit); the sources assert it with this proof sketch, Scholze noting that a precise formulation needs care and working instead with equivariant sites.
proofSteps: (a) The period map is the Grothendieck–Messing map of ET.6a/period-morphisms, étale on the generic fibre. Surjectivity is Gross–Hopkins’ theorem; in the infinite-level language it says that for the basic one-dimensional EL datum the Grothendieck–Messing period map of M_{LT,∞} is onto the whole flag variety, equivalently (through the duality ET.6a/el-duality) that the Hodge–Tate period map of the Drinfeld tower is onto ℙ^{n−1}. The fibres: by the infinite-level moduli description (ET.6a/infinite-level-moduli) the points of M_{LT,∞} over x are the frames of the rational Tate module of one quasi-isogeny class, a GLₙ(F)-torsor, so the fibre at level K is GLₙ(F)/K. D^× acts on the Grothendieck–Messing target through its action on the rational Dieudonné module of the framing object, which is the Brauer–Severi identification; Weil descent is ET.6a/actions-and-weil-descent. Levels K that are not principal congruence subgroups are finite étale quotients by free actions (PerfectoidSpaces P8/free-action-quotient-is-torsor).

(b) Change of level: the level structures at K′ over a point at level K form a K/K′-torsor (ET.6a/lubin-tate-tower API levelTorsor); infinite level and perfectoidness are ET.6a/infinite-level-moduli and ET.6a/perfectoid-limit.

(c) On the infinite-level moduli description a point of M_∞ over x is a framed deformation with a trivialisation α of the rational Tate module V ≅ Fⁿ; two points over the same x have the same (G, ρ) up to unique quasi-isogeny and their frames differ by a unique g ∈ GLₙ(F), giving (x, g) ↦ (x, x·g); the inverse is continuous because it is defined on each compact open coset S ⊂ G by finite-level data, and both sides are diamonds (DiamondsAndVStacks D4).
acceptance: For n = 1, ℙ⁰ is a point, the geometric points of M_{LT,K} form the discrete set F^×/K (Lubin–Tate theory), and (c) is the statement that F^× is an F^×-torsor.
The fibre of π_GH over a point at level K = GLₙ(O_F) has the cardinality of GLₙ(F)/GLₙ(O_F), the set of O_F-lattices in Fⁿ.

For the right G-action, (x,h) ↦ (x,xh) intertwines simultaneous translation of both output factors by g with (x,h) ↦ (xg,g⁻¹hg). Translation of the second output factor alone by k corresponds to (x,h) ↦ (x,hk). D^× acts diagonally on the fibre product and on x alone on the source.

sources.match: The Gross–Hopkins period map at finite level is an étale covering with fibres GLₙ(F)/K, D^×-equivariant for the Brauer–Severi identification and Weil-equivariant; the perfectoid infinite level maps to ℙ^{n−1} as a GLₙ(F)-torsor in a sense the paper handles through equivariant sites.
Recalls the period maps with fibres GLₙ(F)/K, their D^× and Weil equivariance, and that the perfectoid limit is a pro-étale GLₙ(F)-torsor over ℙ^{n−1}.
Uses the diamond isomorphism of the fibre product of M_∞ over ℙ^{n−1}_{ℂ_p} with M_∞ × G and its iterates.

nodes.title: Connected components of the Lubin–Tate and Drinfeld towers (Strauch)
nodes.statement: With the notation of SZ.0/gross-hopkins-torsor and C a complete algebraically closed extension of F̆: (a) for m ≥ 1 and K_m = 1 + ϖ^m Mₙ(O_F), the height-zero geometric connected components of M_{LT,K_m} form (O_F/ϖ^m)^×. In Strauch’s finite-level labelling the three factors act through det(g), Nrd(b)⁻¹ and χ_LT(τ)⁻¹; χ_LT is the Lubin–Tate character. At K₀ = GLₙ(O_F) the height-zero space is connected. Including all heights gives a torsor under F^×/(1 + ϖ^m O_F) for m ≥ 1, and under F^×/O_F^× for m = 0. (b) At infinite level π₀(M_{LT,∞,C}) is topologically F^×. With the right G-action and left D^×-action used for ℱ_π, choose the inverse of Strauch’s label when required by the left/right-action conversion: right g translates the label by det(g), and left d by Nrd(d); at C = ℂ_p the Weil descent action translates it by Art_F(w)⁻¹, with Art_F : W_F^ab ≃ F^× sending geometric Frobenius to a uniformiser. Equivalently, the associated sheaf of δ∘det has degree-zero character δ(Nrd(d))δ(Art_F(w))⁻¹, as in DPS Lemma 7.4. (c) Transport the geometric component computation through ET.6a/el-duality, with its group-action dictionary, to the Drinfeld tower. For n = 2 the scalar diag(ϖ,ϖ) shifts height by 2, so the components after its central quotient form F^×/ϖ^{2ℤ}. In particular H⁰_ét(M^p_{Dr,∞}, k_L) ≅ C⁰(ℚ_p^×/p^{2ℤ}, k_L), and C⁰(ℚ_p^×, k_L) is continuously coinduced from C⁰(ℤ_p^× ⊔ pℤ_p^×, k_L) for the height-shift-by-two action of p^ℤ.
hypotheses: Strauch computes the height-zero finite-level spaces; add heights using elements with non-zero determinant valuation, and then take the compatible limit.

Finite-level source labels and the right-G/left-D convention are distinguished explicitly. In left-G/left-D notation the diagonal centre acts trivially; converting G to a right action gives z·x = x·z for central z. The Weil action is used only over ℂ_p. The Artin map is the inverse of the geometric-normalised reciprocity isomorphism from ClassFieldTheory Layer 9.

The degree-zero normalisation is that of DPS Lemmas 7.3–7.4. SCH18 Proposition 4.7 and CDN23 Theorem 3.1(4) print an inverse reduced-norm factor incompatible with that normalisation (source issue E4).
proofSteps: The determinant morphism to the height-one Lubin–Tate tower: the n-th exterior power of the universal formal module is a height-one formal O_F-module, so a Drinfeld level-ϖ^m structure induces a primitive ϖ^m-torsion point of the Lubin–Tate formal module, giving M_{K_m} → Spf(Ŏ_{F,m}) with Ŏ_{F,m} the ring of the Lubin–Tate extension of level m (Strauch Theorem 3.3, Theorem 4.3).

The fibres of this map over C are connected (Strauch Theorem 4.3 via normality of the deformation rings, Proposition 4.2), so π₀ is Gal(F̆_m/F̆) ≅ (O_F/ϖ^m)^× by the Lubin–Tate character (LubinTate LT.2/lt-character, LT.2/reciprocity-comparison).

Equivariance: GLₙ(O_F) acts on the n-th exterior power through det; o_D^× through Nrd⁻¹ (computed on CM points by local class field theory); the Galois group through the inverse Lubin–Tate character (Strauch Theorem 4.4).

Pass to all heights and then the compatible infinite-level determinant map to identify the component space with F^×. Convert each geometric action together with the convention for pullback on sections; evaluation of a section f with f(xg)=π(g⁻¹)f(x) then gives π(Nrd(d)Art_F(w)⁻¹) on S⁰. This also follows for characters directly from DPS Lemma 7.4. Transport the geometric identification by ET.6a/el-duality with its action dictionary; the scalar height shift is ±2 depending on labelling, giving the same quotient F^×/ϖ^{2ℤ}.
acceptance: For n = 1, degree-zero cohomology has d ∈ D^× = F^× acting as π(d) and w acting as π(Art_F(w)⁻¹), so the central-character and twisting formulas agree.
At level K₀ = GLₙ(O_F) the height-zero part is connected (an open (n − 1)-ball), and π₀(M_{LT,K₀,C}) ≅ F^×/O_F^× ≅ ℤ by the height.
The element diag(ϖ, …, ϖ) ∈ G acts on π₀(M_{LT,∞,C}) = F^× by multiplication by ϖⁿ, so it moves the height by n.

nodes.title: Admissible representations of compact p-adic Lie groups: Serre subcategory and finite cohomology
nodes.statement: Let (A, 𝔪) be a complete noetherian local ring with finite residue field of characteristic p and H a p-adic Lie group; call a smooth A[H]-module V admissible if V = ∪_{K, i} V^K[𝔪^i] (K ⊂ H compact open, i ≥ 1) and every V^K[𝔪^i] is a finitely generated A/𝔪^i-module. Then: (a) admissible A[H]-modules form an abelian Serre subcategory of the smooth A[H]-modules; for H compact and V killed by a power of 𝔪, V is admissible iff its Pontryagin dual V^∨ is a finitely generated module over the noetherian ring A[[H]]; (b) if H = K is compact and V is admissible and killed by 𝔪^i, the continuous cohomology groups H^j_cont(K, V) (V discrete) are finitely generated A/𝔪^i-modules for all j ≥ 0, in particular finite; (c) the restriction of an admissible A[H]-module to an open subgroup of H is admissible.
hypotheses: (A, 𝔪) complete noetherian local with finite residue field of characteristic p; H a p-adic Lie group (locally ℚ_p-analytic), K compact open.

Restriction to a closed subgroup that is not open (such as SL₂(F) ⊂ GL₂(F)) need not preserve admissibility without further hypotheses; the case used later (a central character) is treated in SZ.2/fust-cohomology.
The sources state (b) for 𝔽_p-coefficients (Scholze) and O/ϖⁿ-coefficients (Fust), and cite Emerton for (a); the general A/𝔪^i case is the same argument, recorded here.
proofSteps: (a) Noetherianity: by the Cohen structure theorem A is a quotient of W(k)[[x₁, …, x_r]] (DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra R03.1/cohen-series-presentation), so A[[K]] is a quotient of W(k) ⊗_{ℤ_p} ℤ_p[[K × ℤ_p^r]], noetherian by Lazard’s theorem for the compact p-adic Lie group K × ℤ_p^r (NE.0/iwasawa-noetherian) and finiteness of W(k) over ℤ_p. Duality: Pontryagin duality exchanges smooth 𝔪-power-torsion A[K]-modules with compact A[[K]]-modules; for V killed by 𝔪^i, V is admissible iff V[𝔪] is (Emerton Lemma 2.2.11), and V^∨ is finitely generated iff V^∨/𝔪V^∨ = V[𝔪]^∨ is (topological Nakayama), which reduces to the residue field, the compact-to-smooth direction of CC.5/smooth-dual-admissibility. For the converse over the finite residue field, choose generators of the dual of V^K for a sufficiently small open normal pro-p K and lift them to V^∨; topological Nakayama gives finite generation over k[[K]], hence over k[[H]]. The Pontryagin dual here is Hom_cont over ℤ_p with values in ℚ_p/ℤ_p, with its contragredient A-action; construct its comparison with Mathlib’s circle-valued multiplicative PontryaginDual and biduality on these torsion/compact categories. CC.5 alone does not provide an A-linear anti-equivalence. Finitely generated modules over a noetherian ring form a Serre subcategory, and admissibility is tested on one compact open subgroup. For A = O_L this notion is ModpRepresentations MP.0/torsion-admissibility, and for A = k it agrees with SmoothRepresentations’ admissibility (finite-dimensional invariants).

(b) Continuous cohomology of the compact group K with discrete coefficients is the derived functor of K-invariants on smooth modules (SR.0 derived invariants); resolve V^∨ by finite free A/𝔪^i[[K]]-modules (noetherianity), dualise to an injective resolution of V by duals of finite free modules, whose K-invariants are finite A/𝔪^i-modules; so the cohomology is finitely generated (Scholze Lemma 3.13, Fust Lemma 6.2).
acceptance: For K = ℤ_p and V = 𝔽_p trivial, H⁰ = H¹ = 𝔽_p and H^j = 0 for j ≥ 2.
For V = C⁰(K, 𝔽_p) (the smooth regular representation, admissible), H^j_cont(K, V) = 0 for j > 0 and H⁰ = 𝔽_p (Shapiro).
The non-admissible V = C⁰(K, 𝔽_p)^{⊕ℕ} has infinite H⁰ = 𝔽_p^{⊕ℕ}, so admissibility cannot be dropped in (b).
For a compact p-adic Lie group, the trivial representation on 𝔽_p is admissible; the zero representation is admissible.

The discrete trivial representation on a countably infinite direct sum of copies of 𝔽_p is smooth and is not admissible, since every compact-open fixed space is the entire infinite-dimensional module.

sources.match: Admissible A[G]-modules over a complete noetherian local ring with finite residue field, and Emerton’s result that they form an abelian Serre subcategory of the smooth modules.

For a compact p-adic Lie group and an admissible smooth 𝔽_p-representation, continuous cohomology is finite-dimensional, via the derived-functor description, the duality with finitely generated Iwasawa modules and Lazard’s noetherianity.

For a compact p-adic analytic group and an admissible representation over O/ϖ^n, the continuous cohomology groups are finitely generated O/ϖ^n-modules, by a resolution of the dual by finite free O/ϖ^n[[K]]-modules.

nodes.title: Scholze’s sheaf ℱ_π on projective space
nodes.statement: Let F/ℚ_p be finite, n ≥ 1, G = GLₙ(F), D the division algebra of invariant 1/n, M_{LT,∞} → ℙ^{n−1}_{F̆} the Gross–Hopkins torsor (SZ.0/gross-hopkins-torsor), and (A, 𝔪) a complete noetherian local ring with finite residue field of characteristic p. For a smooth A[G]-module π (every vector has open stabiliser and is killed by a power of 𝔪; π carries the discrete topology), define a presheaf ℱ_π on the equivariant site (ℙ^{n−1}_{F̆}/D^×)_ét by ℱ_π(U) = the A-module of continuous maps f : |U ×_{ℙ^{n−1}} M_{LT,∞}| → π with f(x·g) = g⁻¹·f(x) for g ∈ G and f(d·x) = f(x) for d ∈ D^× (equivalently, after pullback to (ℙ^{n−1})_ét, ℱ_π(U) = C⁰_G(|U_∞|, π) = (π_{GH,∗}π̲)^G(U) with U_∞ = U ×_{ℙ^{n−1}} M_{LT,∞}). Then ℱ_π is a sheaf of A-modules, equivariant for the Weil descent datum; π ↦ ℱ_π is an exact A-linear functor commuting with filtered colimits; and for every geometric point x̄ of ℙ^{n−1}_{F̆} with a chosen lift x̃ to M_{LT,∞}, evaluation at x̃ is an isomorphism (ℱ_π)_{x̄} ≅ π, functorial in π (changing x̃ to x̃·g composes with π(g⁻¹)).
hypotheses: π smooth; the stalk formula and exactness use smoothness (for a non-smooth discrete π the stalk is the submodule of smooth vectors).
The right action of G on M_{LT,∞} is turned into a left action on π-valued functions by g ↦ g⁻¹; D^× acts trivially on π.
proofSteps: Sheaf property: étale covers are open and jointly surjective on topological spaces, so continuous G-equivariant maps glue (Scholze Proposition 3.1); Weil equivariance is inherited from the period map.
Pullback to (ℙ^{n−1})_ét is computed by the limit formula of SZ.0/equivariant-site-toolkit (a): a G-equivariant map on a qcqs U_∞ is automatically invariant under an open subgroup of D^×.

Stalks: for a cofinal system of connected affinoid étale neighbourhoods U_i of x̄, G acts transitively on π₀(|U_i,∞|), so evaluation at x̃ is injective; choosing U_i to factor through M_{LT,K_m} (K_m = 1 + ϖ^m Mₙ(O_F)) gives a G-equivariant surjection |U_i,∞| → G/K_m, through which any K_m-fixed vector extends, so evaluation is surjective onto π^{K_m} for every m, hence onto π when π is smooth (Scholze Proposition 3.1).
Exactness and colimits: tested on stalks after pullback, using conservativity (SZ.0/equivariant-site-toolkit (c)).
acceptance: For n = 1, ℙ⁰ is a point and global sections of ℱ_π are π.
For π the trivial representation A, ℱ_A is the constant sheaf A.
The stalk isomorphism is natural in π; changing x̃ to x̃g multiplies evaluation by π(g⁻¹).

sources.match: The presheaf of continuous GLₙ(F) × D^×-equivariant maps from the pullback of U to M_{LT,∞} into π is a Weil-equivariant sheaf on (ℙ^{n−1}/D^×)_ét; π ↦ ℱ_π is exact and its geometric fibres are π, canonically after choosing a lift to M_{LT,∞}.
ℱ_π = (π_{GH,∗}π̲)^{GLₙ(F)} with ℱ_π(U) = C⁰_{GLₙ(F)}(|U_∞|, π), geometric fibres π for smooth π, the identification depending functorially on a lift of the geometric point.

the pullback of ℱ_π to M_∞ × G^k is the pullback of the constant sheaf π, giving the Cartan–Leray spectral sequence

nodes.title: Scholze’s functors Sⁱ
nodes.statement: With the notation of SZ.1/scholze-sheaf, let C be a complete algebraically closed extension of F̆ and set Sⁱ_C(π) := Hⁱ_ét(ℙ^{n−1}_C, ℱ_π). The equivariant structure makes this an A[D^×]-module, smooth because it is the colimit of Hⁱ((ℙ^{n−1}_C/K)_ét, ℱ_π) over compact open K ⊂ D^×. At C = ℂ_p write Sⁱ(π); it also has the commuting W_F-action supplied by inertia on ℂ_p and the Weil descent datum. The Sⁱ_C form an A-linear cohomological δ-functor and commute with filtered colimits; the long exact sequence is W_F-equivariant when C = ℂ_p. For O = O_L and M in C_G(O), the Pontryagin-dual category of locally admissible smooth O-torsion G-representations, define Šⁱ(M) := Sⁱ(M^∨)^∨, with M^∨ = Hom_cont,O(M,L/O). These dual functors form a covariant homological δ-functor commuting with projective limits in that category.
hypotheses: A and π as in SZ.1/scholze-sheaf; when π is admissible, SZ.1/scholze-finiteness shows that Sⁱ(π) does not depend on C.
Sⁱ(π) is not the π-isotypic part of the cohomology of the tower: the two are compared in SZ.2/comparison-map.

An arbitrary algebraically closed C/F̆ is not equipped here with a canonical W_F-action. The dual coefficient field L and valuation ring O_L are fixed; general A-linear duality is not identified with Hom_cont(−,L/O). C_G(O) has the inverse-limit topology and continuous compatible G-action coming from this dual category.
proofSteps: Define Sⁱ by étale cohomology of the sheaf pulled back to ℙ^{n−1}_C; the D^×-action comes from the equivariant site and is smooth by the limit formula SZ.0/equivariant-site-toolkit (a).

The δ-functor structure follows from exactness of π ↦ ℱ_π (SZ.1/scholze-sheaf) and the long exact cohomology sequence; compatibility with filtered colimits holds because the étale site of the qcqs space ℙ^{n−1}_C is coherent, and cohomology on a coherent site commutes with filtered colimits of sheaves (DiamondsAndVStacks D0/filtered-colimits-and-cohomology-on-coherent-sites).

For O = O_L use the coefficient-linear Pontryagin duality constructed in SZ.0/compact-lie-admissible-cohomology, specialised to Hom_cont,O(−,L/O). On C_G(O) and its smooth torsion dual category it exchanges projective limits and filtered colimits and is exact, so applying it twice to Sⁱ gives the homological δ-functor (DPS §7). Mathlib’s PontryaginDual is the underlying circle-valued construction, not this entire equivalence.
acceptance: For n = 1, S⁰(π) = π and Sⁱ(π) = 0 for i > 0.
For n = 2 and π = 𝔽_p, S⁰ = 𝔽_p, S¹ = 0 and S² = 𝔽_p(−1) as a Galois module, with D^× acting trivially.
A short exact sequence 0 → χ → Ind_B^G χ → St ⊗ χ → 0 gives the long exact sequence used in SZ.3/ludwig-vanishing.

nodes.title: Almost finiteness of restriction to strictly contained opens
nodes.statement: Let C be a complete algebraically closed extension of ℚ_p, V a separated smooth quasicompact adic space over Spa(C, O_C) and U ⊂ V a quasicompact open subset strictly contained in V (for every maximal point x = Spa(K, O_K) of U and every open bounded valuation subring K⁺ ⊂ K, the map Spa(K, O_K) → U extends to Spa(K, K⁺) → V). Then for every i ≥ 0 the image of Hⁱ(V_ét, O⁺/p) → Hⁱ(U_ét, O⁺/p) is an almost finitely generated O_C-module.
hypotheses: V separated, smooth and quasicompact; no properness and no global good coordinates are assumed.
proofSteps: Affinoid case with good coordinates (V → 𝕋ⁿ a composite of finite étale maps and rational embeddings, U ⊂ V strict rational): this is the local lemma of the primitive comparison theorem (P8:local-rational/primitive-local-cohomology).

Affinoid case in general: choose a finite cover U = ∪ U_j with rational V_j ⊂ V having good coordinates and U_j ⊂ V_j strict, and N ≥ i + 2 intermediate strict rational subsets U_j = U_j^{(N)} ⊂ … ⊂ U_j^{(1)} = V_j; compare the Čech spectral sequences of the N covers and apply the finite-image propagation lemma (P8:local-rational/finite-image-spectral-sequence).

Existence of the cover: for a maximal point x ∈ U the closure of x in V is the Riemann–Zariski space of K(x) (separatedness and strictness), so by Temkin’s criterion x has an affinoid neighbourhood containing its closure; shrink it to have good coordinates (Scholze 2013 Lemma 5.2) and take a strict rational neighbourhood inside U; quasicompactness gives a finite subcover.
General quasicompact separated V: run the same argument with affinoid V_j, intersections being affinoid by separatedness.
acceptance: For V proper smooth and U = V this is the almost finite generation of Hⁱ(V, O⁺/p) in the primitive comparison theorem.
For V the closed unit disc over C, H¹_ét(V, 𝔽_p) is infinite-dimensional and depends on C (Scholze, Remark 1.2, p. 3), so the passage to a strictly contained U cannot be omitted.

sources.locator: Definition 3.4, Lemma 3.5 and Corollary 3.6 with proof, pp. 12–13

nodes.title: Almost modules with Frobenius structure are almost free (Scholze 2013 Lemma 2.12)
nodes.statement: Let K be a complete algebraically closed non-archimedean field of characteristic p with valuation ring O and pseudo-uniformiser π, and for every k ≥ 1 let M_k be an O/π^k-module such that: (i) M₁ is almost finitely generated; (ii) there are maps p_k : M_{k+1} → M_k and q_k : M_k → M_{k+1} with p_k ∘ q_k = π, and M₁ → M_{k+1} → M_k (the first map q_k ∘ ⋯ ∘ q₁) is exact in the middle; (iii) there are isomorphisms φ_k : M_k ⊗_{O/π^k, φ} O/π^{pk} ≅ M_{pk} compatible with the p_k and q_k. Then there are r ≥ 0 and isomorphisms of almost modules M_k^a ≅ (O^a/π^k)^r for all k carrying p_k to the projection, q_k to multiplication by π and φ_k to the coordinatewise Frobenius.
hypotheses: K algebraically closed of characteristic p (in the application, the tilt C^♭ of C, with π = p^♭); almost mathematics relative to the maximal ideal of O.
proofSteps: Use the sequence γ(M) = (γ₁,γ₂,…) of elementary divisors for almost finitely generated torsion modules and its majorisation inequality, as constructed in SCH13 Propositions 2.10–2.11. It is not a single length invariant.

Condition (ii) gives γ(M_k) ≤ kγ(M₁) in majorisation order; Frobenius gives γ(M_{pk}) = pγ(M_k). Comparing along arbitrarily high p-powers forces equality γ(M_k)=kγ(M₁). Proposition 2.11(v) then shows that the kernel and cokernel errors are almost zero, giving exact sequences 0 → M₁^a → M_{k+1}^a → M_k^a → 0 and their iterates.
For M = lim_k M_k, these exact sequences identify M^a/π^k with M_k^a and show flatness. Lemma 2.13 gives almost finite generation from π-adic completeness and the almost finite generation modulo π.

The induced Frobenius on M ⊗ K defines an étale 𝔽_p-local system over the algebraically closed field K, hence a trivial finite-rank Frobenius module. Bound the image lattice M′ between π^m O^r and π⁻ᵐ O^r and apply inverse Frobenius repeatedly; the exponents tend to zero, proving M′^a ≅ (O^a)^r compatibly with Frobenius. Reduce modulo π^k (SCH13, end of the proof of Lemma 2.12, p. 13).
acceptance: For M_k = (O/π^k)^r with the obvious maps the lemma is an identity.
For M_k = 0 for all k one gets r = 0.
The family M_k = O/π (constant) violates γ(M_{pk}) = pγ(M_k), so condition (iii) cannot hold for it: the Frobenius structure is what forces freeness.

sources.locator: Propositions 2.10–2.11 and Lemmas 2.12–2.13 with the conclusion of the proof, pp. 10–13
sources.match: For O/π^k-modules M_k over an algebraically closed field of characteristic p with M₁ almost finitely generated, transition maps as in (ii) and Frobenius isomorphisms as in (iii), M_k^a ≅ (O^a/π^k)^r compatibly with all the structure.
Applies Scholze 2013 Lemma 2.12 to Hⁱ((ℙ^{n−1}_C/K)_ét, ℱ_π ⊗ O^♭⁻[(p^♭)^k]) to obtain Hⁱ(ℱ_π ⊗ O⁺/p) ≅^a (O_C^a/p)^r compatibly with Frobenius.

nodes.title: Scholze’s finiteness theorem for Sⁱ
nodes.statement: Let (A, 𝔪) be a complete noetherian local ring with finite residue field of characteristic p, π an admissible A[GLₙ(F)]-module (SZ.0/compact-lie-admissible-cohomology) and C a complete algebraically closed extension of F̆. Then for every i ≥ 0: (1) Sⁱ_C(π) is an admissible A[D^×]-module, and for C ⊂ C′ the natural map Sⁱ_C(π) → Sⁱ_{C′}(π) is an isomorphism; (2) the natural map Sⁱ(π) ⊗_{ℤ_p} O_C → Hⁱ_ét(ℙ^{n−1}_C, ℱ_π ⊗_{ℤ_p} O⁺) is an almost isomorphism of O_C-modules (for π killed by p this reads Sⁱ(π) ⊗_{𝔽_p} O_C/p ≅^a Hⁱ_ét(ℙ^{n−1}_C, ℱ_π ⊗ O⁺/p)); (3) Sⁱ(π) = 0 for i > 2(n − 1), and if π is killed by p and injective as a smooth GLₙ(O_F)-representation then Sⁱ(π) = 0 for i > n − 1; (4) if π is killed by p, then for every compact open K ⊂ D^× the groups Hⁱ((ℙ^{n−1}_C/K)_ét, ℱ_π) are finite.
hypotheses: π admissible in Emerton’s sense; nothing is asserted for non-admissible π, whose Sⁱ need not be admissible.
Almost mathematics is taken with respect to the maximal ideal of O_C (PerfectoidSpaces P0).
proofSteps: Local finiteness (Scholze Lemma 3.7): on an affinoid V ⊂ ℙ^{n−1} with a section to M_{LT,0} and a strict rational U ⊂ V, resolve an admissible GLₙ(O_F)-representation π₀ killed by p by finite sums of π_reg = C⁰(GLₙ(O_F), 𝔽_p) (duality with finitely generated modules over the noetherian 𝔽_p[[GLₙ(O_F)]], SZ.0/compact-lie-admissible-cohomology); exactness of π ↦ ℱ_π and the finite-image propagation lemma reduce to π_reg.

For π_reg (Scholze Lemma 3.8), Rα_∗(O⁺_{V_∞/K}/p) ≅ ℱ_{π_reg} ⊗ O⁺/p for α : (V_∞/K)_ét → (V/K)_ét; through the duality isomorphism M_{LT,∞} ≅ M_{Dr,∞} (ET.6a/el-duality) and the tower equivalence (SZ.0/equivariant-site-toolkit (d)) V_∞/K descends to an open V_K ⊂ M_{Dr,K} (ET.6a/drinfeld-tower; for K ⊂ O_D^× not a principal congruence subgroup, M_{Dr,K} is the quotient of a principal level by a free finite action, PerfectoidSpaces P8/free-action-quotient-is-torsor), separated, smooth and quasicompact because the Drinfeld levels are finite étale over the open subspace Ω^{n−1} of ℙ^{n−1} and V is quasicompact; so the cohomology becomes Hⁱ(V_{K,C}, O⁺/p); SZ.1/strict-image-almost-finite applies to U_K ⊂ V_K.

Global almost finiteness (Corollaries 3.9–3.10): cover ℙ^{n−1} by enough nested pairs U ⊂ V, compare Čech spectral sequences with the finite-image propagation lemma, and pass from a small K′ to K with the Hochschild–Serre spectral sequence of K/K′.

Finiteness and the almost isomorphism (Corollary 3.11): build O^♭⁻ as a Frobenius-twisted colimit of O⁺/p on the étale site; after checking exactness of the Frobenius-twisted colimit and its Frobenius isomorphisms on the pro-étale site after tilting (PerfectoidSpaces P3/etale-site-tilting-equivalence), the Frobenius almost-module lemma (SZ.1/frobenius-almost-module-lemma) gives Hⁱ(ℱ_π ⊗ O⁺/p) ≅^a (O_C^a/p)^r compatibly with Frobenius, and the Artin–Schreier sequence 0 → ℱ_π → ℱ_π ⊗ O^♭⁻ → ℱ_π ⊗ O^♭⁻ → 0 gives Hⁱ((ℙ^{n−1}_C/K)_ét, ℱ_π) ≅ 𝔽_p^r.

Admissibility and independence of C (Corollary 3.14): pass to the colimit over K (SZ.0/equivariant-site-toolkit (a)); base change of affinoid perfectoid spaces gives invariance under C ⊂ C′ of the O⁺/p-cohomology up to almost isomorphism; admissibility by induction on i using the Hochschild–Serre spectral sequence (SZ.0/equivariant-site-toolkit (e)) and finiteness of continuous cohomology of K with admissible coefficients (SZ.0/compact-lie-admissible-cohomology (b)).

Vanishing (end of §3): |ℙ^{n−1}_C| has cohomological dimension n − 1, and Rⁱλ_∗(ℱ_π ⊗ O⁺/p) is almost zero for i > n − 1 because after pullback to M_{LT,0,C} (local sections of π_GH) ℱ_π is a filtered colimit of 𝔽_p-local systems (P8:local-rational/primitive-local-cohomology); for π injective over GLₙ(O_F) reduce to π_reg, where the preimages in M_{LT,∞} of a basis of affinoids of M_{LT,0,C} are affinoid perfectoid and O⁺/p is almost acyclic on them (PerfectoidSpaces P3/etale-almost-acyclicity).

General A (Scholze Theorem 4.4): dévissage along 0 → π[𝔪] → π → π/π[𝔪] → 0 for π killed by a power of 𝔪, then the colimit over 𝔪^j-torsion with an induction on i, using that admissible modules form a Serre subcategory (SZ.0/compact-lie-admissible-cohomology (a)).
acceptance: For n = 1 the theorem says that π is admissible as a D^× = F^×-module, which is the hypothesis.
For n = 2, F = ℚ_p and π = 𝔽_p, Sⁱ(π) is 𝔽_p, 0, 𝔽_p(−1) in degrees 0, 1, 2 (finite, hence admissible), and vanishes in degree 3.
For n = 2 every admissible π has Sⁱ(π) = 0 outside degrees 0, 1, 2; SZ.3/ludwig-vanishing shows that degree 2 also vanishes on principal series of GL₂(ℚ_p).

sources.locator: Theorem 3.2, p. 11; Lemmas 3.7–3.8, pp. 13–15; Corollaries 3.9–3.11, pp. 15–16; Lemma 3.12 and Corollary 3.14, pp. 17–18
sources.match: The 𝔽_p-case: admissibility of Hⁱ_ét(ℙ^{n−1}_C, ℱ_π), independence of C, the almost isomorphism with O⁺/p-cohomology, vanishing above 2(n − 1) and above n − 1 for GLₙ(O)-injective π, proved by local finiteness through the Drinfeld side, Artin–Schreier for O^♭⁻ and an induction with Hochschild–Serre.
The extension to admissible A[GLₙ(F)]-modules over a complete noetherian local ring with finite residue field, with the almost isomorphism Sⁱ ⊗_{ℤ_p} O_C ≅^a Hⁱ(ℱ_V ⊗ O⁺).
Restates Scholze’s results: Sⁱ(π) is an admissible A[D_p^×]-module, the almost isomorphism with O⁺-coefficients, and vanishing for i > 2(n − 1).

nodes.title: Galois action, degree zero, central characters and twists for Sⁱ
nodes.statement: Let (A, 𝔪) and π be as in SZ.1/scholze-finiteness, C = ℂ_p. (a) The action of W_F on Sⁱ(π) (inertia through ℂ_p, Frobenius through the Weil descent datum) is continuous for the discrete topology and extends uniquely to a continuous action of Gal_F = Gal(F̄/F), commuting with D^×. (b) The map S⁰(π^{SLₙ(F)}) → S⁰(π) is an isomorphism, and S⁰(π) ≅ π^{SLₙ(F)} as A-modules, W_F × D^× acting through the homomorphism W_F × D^× → F^× ≅ GLₙ(F)/SLₙ(F) (via det) given by (w,d) ↦ Art_F(w)⁻¹Nrd(d), with geometric Frobenius mapped to a uniformiser by Art_F; in particular S⁰(π) = 0 whenever π^{SLₙ(F)} = 0. (c) If the centre F^× of GLₙ(F) acts on π by a character ζ, the centre F^× of D^× acts on every Sⁱ(π) by ζ. (d) For a smooth character δ : F^× → A^×, there are natural isomorphisms of Gal_F × D^×-modules Sⁱ(π ⊗ δ∘det) ≅ Sⁱ(π) ⊗_A (δ⁻¹ ⊠ δ), δ⁻¹ seen on Gal_F through local class field theory and δ on D^× through the reduced norm. (e) For n = 2 and A killed by a power of 𝔪 (so that δ∘det is a smooth A[G]-module): S¹(δ∘det) = 0 and S²(δ∘det) is free of rank one over A with Gal_F × D^× acting by a character.
hypotheses: Normalisation: Art_F : W_F^ab ≃ F^× maps geometric Frobenius to a uniformiser; right G-equivariance of sections is f(xg)=π(g⁻¹)f(x), and D^× acts on them by (d·f)(x)=f(d⁻¹x). Use the common-central-character convention of DPS Lemmas 7.3–7.4; see E4 for the conflicting inverse norm in SCH18/CDN23.
In (e), S²(δ∘det) ≅ A(−1) ⊗ (δ⁻¹ ⊠ δ), from H²(ℙ¹_C, A) ≅ A(−1) and (d).
proofSteps: (a) Reduce to A finite. Continuity of the inertia action: Sⁱ(π) is the colimit of the cohomology over finite extensions M/F̆ inside ℂ_p (cohomology commutes with this limit of spaces). The K-invariants are finite (SZ.1/scholze-finiteness), and a continuous W_F-action on a finite set extends to Gal_F because an open subgroup of inertia acts trivially and a power of Frobenius acts trivially (Scholze Proposition 4.6).

(b) By SZ.0/lubin-tate-components, S⁰(π) is the space of equivariant continuous maps F^× → π. Such maps land in π^{SLₙ(F)}, and evaluation at 1 identifies this space with π^{SLₙ(F)}. For the chosen right G-action f(t)=π(t⁻¹)f(1); pullback by d⁻¹ and w⁻¹ gives π(Nrd(d)Art_F(w)⁻¹). In particular a character δ gives δ⁻¹ ⊠ δ, agreeing with DPS Lemma 7.4 and the central-action proof in (c).

(c) The diagonal F^× ⊂ Z(G) × Z(D^×) acts trivially on M_{LT,∞} (moduli description, ET.6a/actions-and-weil-descent), and sections of ℱ_π are G-equivariant, so the two central actions agree (DPS Lemma 7.3).
(d) The product ℱ_π ⊗ ℱ_δ → ℱ_{π⊗δ} and cup product give Sⁱ(π) ⊗ S⁰(δ∘det) → Sⁱ(π ⊗ δ∘det); S⁰(δ∘det) ≅ δ⁻¹ ⊠ δ by (b); the same construction for δ⁻¹ gives the inverse (DPS Lemma 7.4).
(e) For the trivial character ℱ is constant, so S¹ = H¹(ℙ¹_C, A) = 0 and S² = H²(ℙ¹_C, A) ≅ A(−1); twist by (d).
acceptance: For π = δ∘det with n = 2, S⁰(π) is free of rank one with the character described in (b).
For π a generic principal series of GL₂(ℚ_p) (no SL₂-invariants), S⁰(π) = 0.
Twisting by δ∘det and then by δ⁻¹∘det returns Sⁱ(π) through the identification δ ⊗ δ⁻¹ = 1.
For n=1, F=ℚ₅ and δ(2)=2 in 𝔽₅^×, S⁰(δ) has D^×-central action δ(2)=2; an inverse reduced-norm formula would give 3 and violate (c) and (d).

sources.match: Proposition 4.6 proves the extension of the Weil action to Gal_F; Proposition 4.7 identifies degree zero with SLₙ(F)-invariants using Strauch’s components. The action formula is converted to the DPS common-central-character convention; the printed inverse norm is recorded in E4.
Restates the extension of the W_F-action to 𝒢_F and the computation of S⁰.
The central actions of F^× on Hⁱ_ét(ℙ^{n−1}_{ℂ_p}, ℱ_π) through G and through D^× coincide, and twisting π by δ∘det twists the cohomology by δ⁻¹ ⊠ δ.

sources.match: Uses that S⁰ of a successive extension of characters is a successive extension of characters and that S¹ of the trivial representation vanishes because the attached sheaf is constant; the rank-one statement for S²(δ∘det) in (e) is derived here from (d) and H²(ℙ¹_C, A) ≅ A(−1).

nodes.title: Continuous cohomology of p-adic groups with smooth coefficients (Fust)
nodes.statement: Let G be a locally profinite group, k a commutative ring and π a smooth k[G]-module with the discrete topology, regarded as a continuous representation; Hⁱ(G, −) denotes continuous cohomology computed by continuous homogeneous cochains (Mathlib’s continuousCohomology). (a) There are natural isomorphisms Hⁱ(G, π) ≅ Extⁱ_G(1, π), the Ext groups taken in the abelian category of smooth k[G]-modules. (b) (Shapiro) If H ⊂ G is a closed subgroup such that G → H\G has a continuous section and V is a topological H-module, then Hⁱ(G, Ind_H^G V) ≅ Hⁱ(H, V) for the continuous induction Ind_H^G V = {f ∈ C(G, V) : f(hg) = h·f(g)}. (c) If G is a p-adic reductive group (the F-points of a connected reductive group over a finite extension F/ℚ_p; for instance SL₂(F) or GL₂(F)), O the integers of a finite extension of ℚ_p with uniformiser ϖ, and π an admissible smooth O/ϖⁿ[G]-module, then every Hⁱ(G, π) is a finitely generated O/ϖⁿ-module. (d) If k is a finite field of characteristic p and π is an absolutely irreducible smooth k-representation of GL₂(ℚ_p) that is not isomorphic to the twist by a character of 1, of the Steinberg representation Sp, or of Ind_B^G α with α(diag(a, d)·u) = ω(a)ω(d)⁻¹ (ω the mod p cyclotomic character, so that Ind_B^G α = I(1, ε) in the notation of SZ.4), then Hⁱ(SL₂(ℚ_p), π) = 0 for all i ≥ 0. (e) If π is an admissible smooth k-representation of GL₂(F) with a central character, its restriction to SL₂(F) is admissible.
hypotheses: In (b) the section is continuous (for G = GL₂(F), H = SL₂(F) one can take x ↦ diag(x, 1)); V is any topological H-module, in particular a prodiscrete one.
In (d) the excluded representations are exactly the members of the twists of the block containing the trivial representation; for p ≥ 5 this is the block {χ, St ⊗ χ, I(χ, χε)} of SZ.2/comparison-map.

For (b), Ind has the compact-open topology and the right-translation G-action. For discrete smooth π in (a), TauCeti.IsSmoothDiscrete supplies the joint-continuity/smoothness condition absent from a bare TopRep object.
proofSteps: (a) Apply the functor of smooth vectors to the resolution of π by continuous cochain modules C(G^{n+1}, π); it gives a resolution of π by acyclic objects of the smooth category, because C(G, −)^{sm} is right adjoint to the forgetful functor and preserves injectives, and the G-invariants of the cochains are unchanged (Fust Lemmas 2.1–2.3, 4.1–4.3, Corollary 4.4; for compact G this is Emerton’s Proposition 2.2.6).

(b) Evaluation at the identity gives a cochain map from the continuous G-cochains of Ind_H^G V to the H-cochains of V. A continuous section of H\G constructs an inverse up to cochain homotopy, by the usual insertion homotopies; these maps are continuous for the compact-open topologies. This proves a quasi-isomorphism, rather than a termwise isomorphism of cochain groups (Fust Lemma 2.2). Mathlib’s TopRep.coind₁ supplies the H=1 continuous-function object with action (gf)(x)=g·f(g⁻¹x); untwisting by x⁻¹ on values and switching left/right conventions relates it to continuous induction. General closed-subgroup induction and Shapiro are proved here.

(c) The Schneider–Stuhler resolution of the trivial representation by compact inductions c-Ind_{P_F^†} δ_F from facet stabilisers, built here from the oriented cellular chain complex of the Bruhat–Tits building, exact because the building is contractible (a CAT(0) space, ReductiveGroupsPartII RG2.2/building-metric), with finitely many orbits of facets (RG2.2/building-cocompact-action) and P_F^† containing a compact open normal R_F with ZR_F of finite index (Schneider–Stuhler §1.2 from RG2.2/stabilizers-and-fixers; Fust Lemma 6.5), reduces, through (a) and a double-complex spectral sequence, to the cohomology of the facet stabilisers P_F^†; these are handled by the Hochschild–Serre argument of Fust Lemma 6.3 applied to R_F ⊂ ZR_F ⊂ P_F^† (R_F compact open normal, with finite or finitely generated abelian quotients) and the compact case SZ.0/compact-lie-admissible-cohomology (b) (Fust Lemma 6.6).

(d) First inspect Z ∩ SL₂(ℚ_p). If its scalar action on π is non-trivial, the action of that central element on the group cochain complex is homotopic to the identity, so an invertible non-zero scalar minus 1 annihilates cohomology, forcing vanishing. Otherwise extend ζ_π from Z to Z·SL₂ by making SL₂ act trivially. Exact adjunctions identify Hⁱ(SL₂,π) with Extⁱ_{G,ζ_π}(Ind_{Z·SL₂}^G ζ_π,π). This finite-dimensional induction has character constituents; the block decomposition and Ext comparison from R30.5 show vanishing when π belongs to none of their blocks (Fust Proposition 5.1 and Corollary 5.2).

(e) Take K ⊂ GL₂(O_F) compact open on whose central part ζ is trivial and put K′ = K ∩ SL₂(F); K″ = (Z ∩ K)·K′ is open in GL₂(F) (it is the set of k ∈ K with det k a square of a unit in the image, times SL₂), and π^{K′} = π^{K″} because Z ∩ K acts trivially, so π^{K′} is finite.
acceptance: H⁰(G, π) = π^G and Ext⁰_G(1, π) = Hom_G(1, π) = π^G.
For G = ℤ_p and π = 𝔽_p, H¹ = 𝔽_p and H² = 0, matching Ext¹_{ℤ_p}(𝔽_p, 𝔽_p) = 𝔽_p.
For π supersingular (absolutely irreducible, not in the block of a character), Hⁱ(SL₂(ℚ_p), π) = 0 for all i, while for π = 1 one has H⁰(SL₂(ℚ_p), 1) = k ≠ 0.

sources.match: Continuous group cohomology of a locally profinite group with coefficients in a smooth representation is Ext from the trivial representation in the smooth category.

The case H = 1: continuous equivariant maps into the module induced from the trivial group correspond to continuous maps. The general Shapiro isomorphism for a closed H with a continuous section is Borel–Wallach IX.2.3, which CDN cite (p. 37).

Finite generation of the cohomology of an admissible O/ϖⁿ-representation: first for a group with an open normal subgroup with finitely generated cohomology and finite or finitely generated abelian quotient, then for a p-adic reductive group through the Schneider–Stuhler resolution.

Vanishing of all continuous cohomology of SL₂(ℚ_p) with coefficients in an absolutely irreducible smooth representation of GL₂(ℚ_p) outside the twists of 1, Sp and Ind_B^G α, by block separation of Ext groups.

sources.locator: proof of Corollaire 3.13, p. 37, and proof of Théorème 4.22, p. 46
sources.match: Use Shapiro’s lemma for SL₂ ⊂ GL₂ (the determinant has a continuous section), Fust’s finiteness and vanishing, and that an admissible representation with a central character restricts to an admissible SL₂-representation.

nodes.title: Low-degree cohomology of SL₂(ℚ_p) with trivial mod p coefficients (Moore)
nodes.statement: Let k be a non-archimedean local field and μ(k) its group of roots of unity. For every separable locally compact abelian group A with trivial SL₂(k)-action, H²(SL₂(k), A) ≅ Hom(μ(k), A), where H² classifies topological central extensions (Moore); for A discrete this group is the continuous cohomology H²_cont(SL₂(k), A). Consequently, for p odd: H¹_cont(SL₂(ℚ_p), 𝔽_p) = 0 and H²_cont(SL₂(ℚ_p), 𝔽_p) = 0.
hypotheses: A discrete in the comparison with continuous cochain cohomology; SL₂(k) with its topology as a locally profinite group.
p odd in the consequence: μ(ℚ_p) is cyclic of order p − 1, prime to p.
proofSteps: Build Moore’s rank-one central-extension computation here: SL₂(k) is perfect, and its universal abstract central extension is generated by the rank-one Steinberg generators and relations of Moore Chapter III §§8–9. The resulting Steinberg cocycles have the rank-one symbol relations of Theorem 9.2; these are not identified with the bilinear presentation of stable Milnor K₂. Moore’s local-field uniqueness theorem factors the continuous symbols through the norm-residue symbol, and Theorems 10.3–10.4 identify the topological universal kernel with μ(k). The universal transgression of Theorems 1.1 and 2.3–2.4 gives H² ≅ Hom(μ(k),A). Import the norm-residue pairing from ClassFieldTheory Layer 5.

Comparison for discrete A: the projection of a topological central extension by A is a local homeomorphism. Choose a section near 1 and translate its restriction to a sufficiently small compact-open subgroup over the disjoint clopen cosets of that subgroup; this gives a global continuous section. Its factor set is a continuous cocycle. Conversely a continuous cocycle gives a topological extension, and an equivalence of such extensions is continuous, identifying this classification with continuous-cochain H². No group-homomorphic local splitting is needed.
H¹_cont(SL₂(ℚ_p), 𝔽_p) = Hom_cont(SL₂(ℚ_p), 𝔽_p) = 0 because SL₂(ℚ_p) is perfect; H²_cont(SL₂(ℚ_p), 𝔽_p) ≅ Hom(μ_{p−1}, 𝔽_p) = 0 for p odd.
acceptance: For p = 2, μ(ℚ_2) = {±1} and H²_cont(SL₂(ℚ_2), 𝔽_2) ≅ ℤ/2 ≠ 0, so the oddness of p is needed.
H⁰_cont(SL₂(ℚ_p), 𝔽_p) = 𝔽_p.
The metaplectic double cover of SL₂(ℚ_p) is the pushout of the universal topological extension along μ(ℚ_p) → μ(ℚ_p)/μ(ℚ_p)² ≅ {±1}.

sources.locator: Chapter I, Theorem 1.1, p. 10, and Theorems 2.3–2.4, pp. 15–16
sources.match: For an (abstract) group equal to its commutator subgroup the transgression identifies Hom(π₁(G), A) with H²(G, A); for locally compact groups, with Borel cochains, the topological universal central extension and its universality.

sources.locator: Chapter II, Definition 3.1 and Theorem 3.1, printed pp.17–18 (PDF pp.14–15); Chapter III, Theorems 9.1–9.2, printed pp.46–47 (PDF pp.43–44)
sources.match: The universal rank-one Steinberg relations describe abstract extensions of SL₂; continuity and the local uniqueness theorem force their symbols to factor through the norm-residue symbol. This is the extra input beyond stable Milnor K₂.

For k non-archimedean, H²(SL₂(k), A) ≅ Hom(E_k, A) for every separable locally compact abelian A with trivial action, E_k the roots of unity of k, and π₁ of a simply connected Chevalley group over k is finite cyclic.
Reduces to the vanishing of H²(SL₂(ℚ_p), 𝔽_p), deduced from Moore’s computation of H²(SL₂(ℚ_p), ℝ/ℤ) as the Pontryagin dual of the roots of unity of ℚ_p and the triviality of the abelianisation.

nodes.title: The Cartan–Leray spectral sequence for Scholze’s functor (CDN Theorem 3.2)
nodes.statement: Let F/ℚ_p be finite, n ≥ 1, G = GLₙ(F), M_∞ = M_{LT,∞,ℂ_p}, (A, 𝔪) as in SZ.1/scholze-sheaf and π a smooth admissible A[G]-module killed by p^k. For a Stein affinoid perfectoid exhaustion {U_s}_s of M_∞, the groups H^j_ét(M_∞, π̲) (π̲ the constant sheaf with value π) are prodiscrete: H^j_ét(M_∞, π̲) ≅ lim_s H^j_ét(U_s, π̲) with the discrete topology on each term, and G acts continuously. There is a spectral sequence of D^× × W_F-modules E₂^{ij} = Hⁱ(G, H^j_ét(M_∞, π̲)) ⇒ S^{i+j}(π), where Hⁱ(G, −) is continuous cochain cohomology with prodiscrete coefficients; moreover H^j_ét(M_∞, π̲) = 0 for j ≥ 2.
hypotheses: π admissible and killed by p^k; Stein affinoid perfectoid exhaustions exist by ET.6a/stein-mittag-leffler.
The spectral sequence is in the generality of Scholze’s functor (any F and n), as the source states.
proofSteps: Write U = {M_∞ → ℙ^{n−1}_{ℂ_p}} for the pro-étale cover given by the torsor SZ.0/gross-hopkins-torsor and ν : ℙ_proét → ℙ_ét; the Čech spectral sequence Ȟⁱ(U, H^j(ν^∗ℱ_π)) ⇒ H^{i+j}_proét(ℙ^{n−1}, ν^∗ℱ_π) has abutment Sⁱ⁺ʲ(π) by the comparison of étale and quasi-pro-étale cohomology (DiamondEtaleCohomology C0/quasi-pro-etale-pullback-fully-faithful, Scholze ECD Proposition 14.8).

The (t+1)-fold fibre product of M_∞ over ℙ^{n−1} is M_∞ × G^t and ν^∗ℱ_π pulls back to the constant sheaf π̲ there (SZ.0/gross-hopkins-torsor (c), SZ.1/scholze-sheaf), so the E₁-row j is the complex H^j(M_∞ × G^•, π̲).

Compute H^j(M_∞ × G^t, π̲) ≅ C⁰(G^t, H^j(M_∞, π̲)): cover M_∞ × G^t by U_s × S^t_s with S^t_s compact open exhausting G^t; H^j(U_s × S, π̲) = C⁰(S, ℤ/p^k) ⊗ π ⊗ H^j(U_s, ℤ/p^k) by continuity of étale cohomology along U_s × S = lim U_s × S_m over the finite quotients S_m of S (DiamondEtaleCohomology C0/etale-cohomology-continuity); the systems are Mittag-Leffler (ET.6a/stein-mittag-leffler for {H^j(U_s)}, surjective restriction for C⁰(S, ℤ/p^k)), so the limits commute and give (3.7)–(3.9) of the source.

The identifications are compatible with the Čech differentials (alternating sums of projections, multiplication of G and the action map G × M_∞ → M_∞, all of which map compact pieces into compact pieces), so row j is the continuous cochain complex C⁰(G^•, H^j(M_∞, π̲)) and E₂^{ij} = Hⁱ(G, H^j(M_∞, π̲)).

Vanishing for j ≥ 2: by dévissage reduce to 𝔽_p; on the tilt U_s^♭ (affinoid perfectoid of characteristic p) the Artin–Schreier sequence and the vanishing of H^j(U_s^♭, O) for j ≥ 1 give H^j(U_s, 𝔽_p) = 0 for j ≥ 2; the Milnor sequence with R¹lim H^{j−1}(U_s) = 0 (Mittag-Leffler) gives the vanishing on M_∞.
acceptance: For n = 1, M_∞ = F^× as a profinite-set-indexed union of points, H⁰(M_∞, π̲) = C⁰(F^×, π) = Ind_1^{F^×} π and H^j = 0 for j ≥ 1; Shapiro gives E₂^{i0} = 0 for i > 0 and E₂^{00} = π = S⁰(π).
The edge map S⁰(π) → H⁰(G, H⁰(M_∞, π̲)) is an isomorphism, recovering SZ.1/scholze-galois-and-degree-zero (b) through π₀(M_∞) = F^×.
Exactness in π: a short exact sequence of admissible π gives compatible morphisms of spectral sequences.

The prodiscrete structure of H^q_ét(M_∞, ℤ/p^k) from the Milnor sequence of a Stein affinoid perfectoid cover, and continuous cohomology of G with prodiscrete coefficients as cohomology of continuous cochains.
Mittag-Leffler property of {H^i(U_s, ℤ/p^k)}_s, and the vanishing of H^i(U_s, 𝔽_p) for i ≥ 2 by Artin–Schreier on the tilt.

nodes.title: The spectral sequence in terms of multiplicity spaces (CDN Corollary 3.11)
nodes.statement: In the situation of SZ.2/cartan-leray-spectral-sequence there are natural isomorphisms of prodiscrete G-modules H^j_ét(M_∞, π̲) ≅ Hom^cont_{ℤ_p}(π^∨, H^j_ét(M_∞, ℤ/p^k)), π^∨ the Pontryagin dual (a profinite ℤ_p-module); hence a spectral sequence of D^× × W_F-modules E₂^{ij} = Hⁱ(G, Hom^cont_{ℤ_p}(π^∨, H^j_ét(M_∞, ℤ/p^k))) ⇒ S^{i+j}(π), with only the rows j = 0, 1 non-zero. In particular there is an exact sequence 0 → H¹(G, Hom^cont(π^∨, H⁰_ét(M_∞, ℤ/p^k))) → S¹(π) → Hom^cont_{ℤ_p[G]}(π^∨, H¹_ét(M_∞, ℤ/p^k)) → H²(G, Hom^cont(π^∨, H⁰_ét(M_∞, ℤ/p^k))) → S²(π).
hypotheses: Hom^cont between prodiscrete modules carries the topology lim_j colim_i Hom(U_i, V_j) with discrete Hom(U_i, V_j); for U = lim U_i, V = lim V_j prodiscrete it is again prodiscrete.
proofSteps: On each U_s, π is a filtered colimit of finite ℤ/p^k-modules, so H^j(U_s, π̲) = π ⊗ H^j(U_s, ℤ/p^k) = Hom^cont(π^∨, H^j(U_s, ℤ/p^k)) (U_s qcqs); pass to the limit over s using the Mittag-Leffler property (ET.6a/stein-mittag-leffler).
Substitute into SZ.2/cartan-leray-spectral-sequence; the exact sequence is the five-term sequence of a two-row spectral sequence.
acceptance: For π = ℤ/p^k with trivial action, E₂^{ij} = Hⁱ(G, H^j(M_∞, ℤ/p^k)).
For π killed by p the sequence only involves H^j_ét(M_∞, 𝔽_p).
The middle term Hom^cont_{ℤ_p[G]}(π^∨, H¹_ét(M_∞, ℤ/p^k)) is the multiplicity of π^∨ in the first cohomology of the tower, the object of SZ.5 and SZ.6.

sources.match: The spectral sequence with E₂ = Hⁱ(G, Hom^cont_{ℤ_p}(π^∨, H^j_ét(M_∞, ℤ/p^k))), from H^j_ét(M_∞, π̲) ≅ Hom^cont(π^∨, H^j_ét(M_∞, ℤ/p^k)) computed on a Stein cover.
The low-degree exact sequence obtained from the spectral sequence.

nodes.title: Comparison of S¹(π) with multiplicities in the tower (CDN Corollary 3.13)
nodes.statement: Let F/ℚ_p be finite, G = GL₂(F), M_∞ = M_{LT,∞,ℂ_p} (n = 2), L/ℚ_p finite with residue field k_L, and π a smooth admissible k_L[G]-module with a central character. (a) Hom^cont_{k_L}(π^∨, H⁰_ét(M_∞, k_L)) ≅ Ind_{SL₂(F)}^G π, so V_i(π) := Hⁱ(G, Hom^cont_{k_L}(π^∨, H⁰_ét(M_∞, k_L))) ≅ Hⁱ(SL₂(F), π), finite-dimensional over k_L, and there is an exact sequence 0 → H¹(SL₂(F), π) → S¹(π) → Hom^cont_{k_L[G]}(π^∨, H¹_ét(M_∞, k_L)) → H²(SL₂(F), π). (b) If F = ℚ_p and π is irreducible, the natural map S¹(π) → Hom^cont_{k_L[G]}(π^∨, H¹_ét(M_∞, k_L)) is an isomorphism when no Jordan–Hölder constituent of 𝔽̄_p ⊗_{k_L} π is a twist by a character of 1, of the Steinberg representation or of I(1, ε) (for p ≥ 5: π does not belong to a twist {χ, St ⊗ χ, I(χ, χε)} of the Steinberg block), and in every case its kernel and cokernel are finite-dimensional over k_L.
hypotheses: n = 2; π admissible with a central character (so its restriction to SL₂(F) is admissible, SZ.2/fust-cohomology (e)).

In (b), irreducible over k_L; the reduction to absolutely irreducible representations uses that End_G(π) is a finite extension of k_L over which π is absolutely irreducible (ModpRepresentationsOfGL2OverLocalFields MP.0/scalar-extension).
proofSteps: (a) Take the exact sequence of SZ.2/multiplicity-spectral-sequence with k = 1 and coefficients k_L. By SZ.0/lubin-tate-components π₀(M_∞) = F^× with G acting through det, so H⁰_ét(M_∞, k_L) = C⁰(F^×, k_L) and Hom^cont(π^∨, C⁰(F^×, k_L)) = C⁰(F^×, π) = Ind_{SL₂(F)}^G π; Shapiro’s lemma (SZ.2/fust-cohomology (b)), valid since det has the continuous section x ↦ diag(x, 1), gives V_i(π) ≅ Hⁱ(SL₂(F), π); finiteness is SZ.2/fust-cohomology (c), (e).

(b) Base change to the finite extension k = End_G(π) of k_L, over which k ⊗_{k_L} π splits into Galois-conjugate absolutely irreducible constituents (MP.0/scalar-extension, Lemma 1.7); S¹, continuous cohomology and Hom^cont(−^∨, H¹) commute with this finite free extension of scalars (SZ.1/scholze-functor, baseChange); for the absolutely irreducible constituents outside the Steinberg-type twists, Hⁱ(SL₂(ℚ_p), −) = 0 for all i (SZ.2/fust-cohomology (d)), so V₁ = V₂ = 0 and the map is an isomorphism; otherwise V₁, V₂ are finite-dimensional by (a).
acceptance: For π supersingular and F = ℚ_p the map is an isomorphism.

For π = 1 (trivial), S¹(1) = 0 (SZ.1/scholze-galois-and-degree-zero (e)), so the sequence embeds Hom^cont_G(1, H¹_ét(M_∞, k_L)) into H²(SL₂(ℚ_p), k_L), which vanishes for p odd (SZ.2/moore-sl2-vanishing).
For π = δ∘det a character, H¹(SL₂(F), π) = Hom_cont(SL₂(F), k_L) = 0, so S¹(π) injects into the multiplicity space.

sources.match: For GL₂(ℚ_p) and π smooth admissible irreducible, the map S¹(π) → Hom^cont_{k_L[G]}(π^∨, H¹_ét(M_∞, k_L)) is an isomorphism outside a twist of the Steinberg block and has finite-dimensional kernel and cokernel in general, from (3.14), Shapiro’s lemma and Fust’s results.
The same statement in the introduction, for absolutely irreducible π.
The argument for (3.14) does not use F = ℚ_p and gives 0 → H¹(SL₂(F), π) → S¹(π) → Hom^cont_{k_L[G]}(π^∨, H¹_ét(M_∞, k_L)) → H²(SL₂(F), π) for every F.

nodes.title: The quotient of the Lubin–Tate tower by the Borel subgroup (Ludwig)
nodes.statement: Let n = 2, F = ℚ_p, G = GL₂(ℚ_p), B = B(ℚ_p) the upper-triangular Borel subgroup and M_∞ = M_{LT,∞,ℂ_p} with its right G-action. (a) The quotient M_∞/B, formed in Huber’s category of (pre-)adic spaces from the quotient topological space and the B-invariant sections, is a perfectoid space. The perfectoid space M_B := M^{(0)}_∞/B(ℤ_p) ∼ lim_m M^{(0)}_m/B(ℤ/p^m) is an intermediate quotient. Put G⁰ = {g ∈ G : det(g) ∈ ℤ_p^×} and B′ = B ∩ G⁰, the stabiliser of the height-zero component. The final quotient is M_∞/B ≅ M^{(0)}_∞/B′; its perfectoid charts are open subsets of M_B obtained from local sections of π_GH at level zero. (b) The Gross–Hopkins map factors as π_GH = π̄_GH ∘ q through a quasi-compact map π̄_GH : M_∞/B → ℙ¹_{ℂ_p}; the fibre over a geometric point x is identified with y × ℙ¹(ℚ_p) = y × (B\G) for a lift y of x, and π̄_GH⁻¹(x) is affinoid perfectoid. (c) For a smooth character χ : B → 𝔽_q^×, ℱ_χ(U) = Map_{cont,B}(|U ×_{M_∞/B} M_∞|, χ) is an 𝔽_q-local system of rank one on (M_∞/B)_ét; π̄_{GH,∗}ℱ_χ ≅ ℱ_{Ind_B^G χ}, Rⁱπ̄_{GH,∗}ℱ = 0 for i > 0 and every sheaf ℱ, and hence Sⁱ(Ind_B^G χ) ≅ Hⁱ_ét(M_∞/B, ℱ_χ) for all i.
hypotheses: n = 2 and F = ℚ_p; coefficients are a finite field 𝔽_q of characteristic p. For principal congruence level m use GL₂(ℤ_p) at m=0 and 1+p^mM₂(ℤ_p) for m≥1.
Ind_B^G χ is smooth induction (continuous functions f : G → 𝔽_q with f(bg) = χ(b)f(g)), G/B being compact.
proofSteps: Construct the intermediate perfectoid M_B (Ludwig Theorem 3.11 and Corollary 3.13, pp. 20–22). Serre–Tate uniformisation embeds the height-zero tower into the supersingular locus of the perfectoid modular curve, equivariantly for GL₂(ℤ_p) and compatibly with the Hodge–Tate map (PerfectoidShimuraVarieties S1 request). Quotients by B(ℤ/p^m) and the infinite Γ₀ tower give local perfectoid charts, glued to the tilde-limit M_B. The modular embedding used here is not asserted GL₂(ℚ_p)-equivariant on the height-zero component.

Pass to B′ = B ∩ G⁰ (Ludwig Theorem 3.14, pp. 22–23). Since B = B′ ⋊ ℤ acts transitively on heights, M_∞/B ≅ M^{(0)}_∞/B′. For an affinoid U in height-zero level zero on which π_GH is an isomorphism onto its image, p₀⁻¹(U) ×^{B(ℤ_p)} B′ embeds openly in M^{(0)}_∞; its B′-quotient is p₀⁻¹(U)/B(ℤ_p), an open perfectoid chart in M_B. These charts cover the final quotient. Proposition 3.15 gives quasi-compactness; Propositions 3.17, 3.22 and Lemma 3.23 give its affinoid perfectoid fibres.

For χ trivial on a sufficiently small open subgroup of B(ℤ_p), construct the character sheaf using B-equivariant continuous functions on pullbacks of M_∞. Ludwig Proposition 4.2 proves it is a rank-one local system; this does not require the entire non-quasicompact map M_∞/K → M_∞/B to be étale.

π̄_{GH,∗}ℱ_χ = ℱ_{Ind χ} by Frobenius reciprocity for continuous maps: G-equivariant maps X → Ind_B^G χ correspond to B-equivariant maps X → χ for any G-space X with G/B compact (Ludwig Lemma 4.3) and SZ.1/scholze-sheaf.
Higher direct images: the stalk of Rⁱπ̄_{GH,∗}ℱ at x is the cohomology of the fibre y × ℙ¹(ℚ_p), a profinite set times a geometric point, which vanishes in positive degrees (Ludwig Proposition 4.4).
acceptance: For χ trivial, ℱ_χ is the constant sheaf 𝔽_q and Sⁱ(Ind_B^G 1) = Hⁱ_ét(M_∞/B, 𝔽_q).
The fibre of π̄_GH over a geometric point has π₀ equal to ℙ¹(ℚ_p) = B\G.
Composing with the projection M_∞/B → ℙ¹ recovers the Gross–Hopkins map of SZ.0/gross-hopkins-torsor.

sources.locator: Theorem 3.11, Corollary 3.13, Theorem 3.14 and Proposition 3.15, pp. 20–23; Propositions 3.17 and 3.22, Lemma 3.23, pp. 23–27
sources.match: Constructs the compact B(ℤ_p) intermediate quotient and then glues the B′-quotient of the height-zero component to obtain M_∞/B. Local Gross–Hopkins sections give the perfectoid charts, quasi-compactness and fibre description.

nodes.title: Ludwig’s vanishing theorem for S²
nodes.statement: Let F = ℚ_p, n = 2, G = GL₂(ℚ_p). (a) For smooth characters χ₁, χ₂ : ℚ_p^× → 𝔽_q^×, S²(Ind_B^G(χ₁ ⊗ χ₂)) = 0 (the characters need not be distinct). (b) For every smooth character μ, S²(St ⊗ μ∘det) = 0, St the mod p Steinberg representation. (c) For every smooth character μ, S²(μ∘det) is one-dimensional over 𝔽_q, Gal_{ℚ_p} × D^× acting by a character (from SZ.1/scholze-galois-and-degree-zero (e)). (d) Consequently, if X is a smooth 𝔽_q[G]-module of finite length whose Jordan–Hölder constituents are characters, Steinberg twists or principal series, S²(X) is finite-dimensional and is a successive extension of one-dimensional characters of Gal_{ℚ_p} × D^×; in particular S²(X)^H is a successive extension of Galois characters for every compact open H ⊂ D^×, the form CDN use.
hypotheses: F = ℚ_p and n = 2; coefficients in a finite field of characteristic p.
proofSteps: (a) As S²(Ind χ) is an 𝔽_p-vector space it suffices that S²(Ind χ) ⊗ O_{ℂ_p}/p is almost zero. By SZ.1/scholze-finiteness (2) it is almost isomorphic to H²(ℙ¹, ℱ_{Ind χ} ⊗ O⁺/p) = H²(ℙ¹, π̄_{GH,∗}(ℱ_χ ⊗ O⁺/p)) = H²(M_∞/B, ℱ_χ ⊗ O⁺/p) (SZ.3/borel-quotient (c)).

Compute the last group through π̄_GH : (M_∞/B)_ét → |ℙ¹_{ℂ_p}|: the stalks of the higher direct images are cohomology of the affinoid perfectoid fibres, almost zero in positive degrees (PerfectoidSpaces P3/etale-almost-acyclicity); and sheaf cohomology on |ℙ¹_{ℂ_p}| vanishes above degree 1 (cohomological dimension of the underlying space of a rigid curve). Hence H² is almost zero (Ludwig Theorem 4.6).
(b) From 0 → μ∘det → Ind_B^G(μ ⊗ μ) → St ⊗ μ → 0 and the long exact sequence, S²(Ind) → S²(St ⊗ μ) → S³(μ∘det) = 0 (SZ.1/scholze-finiteness (3)) and S²(Ind) = 0 (Ludwig Corollary 4.7).
(c) SZ.1/scholze-galois-and-degree-zero (e).
(d) Induction on the length: for 0 → X′ → X → X″ → 0 the sequence S²(X′) → S²(X) → S²(X″) → S³(X′) = 0 is exact, so S²(X) is an extension of S²(X″) by a quotient of S²(X′); conclude with (a)–(c).
acceptance: S²(Ind_B^G(1 ⊗ 1)) = 0 although S²(1) ≠ 0: the vanishing is special to inductions.
For a generic pair (χ₁, χ₂) and the non-split extension Π_{χ₁,χ₂} of I(χ₂, χ₁) by I(χ₁, χ₂), S²(Π_{χ₁,χ₂}) = 0.
S²(St) = 0 and S²(1) ≅ 𝔽_q(−1) give, from 0 → 1 → Ind_B^G 1 → St → 0, the exact sequence S¹(St) → S²(1) → S²(Ind_B^G 1) = 0, so S¹(St) ≠ 0.

S²(St ⊗ μ) = 0, from exactness of π ↦ ℱ_π and the vanishing of S³.
Uses Ludwig’s theorem for S²(I(χ₁, χ₂)) = S²(I(χ₂, χ₁)) = 0.

S² kills the Steinberg twists and the parabolic inductions and turns characters into characters, so S²(X)^H is a successive extension of characters as a Galois module; statements (c) and (d) are derived here from (a), (b) and SZ.1/scholze-galois-and-degree-zero (e).

nodes.title: Globalisation of a residual local representation (Gee–Kisin, Dospinescu–Paškūnas–Schraen)
nodes.statement: Let p > 2, L/ℚ_p finite with residue field k_L, [k_L : 𝔽_p] ≥ 2, and r̄ : Gal_{ℚ_p} → GL₂(k_L) continuous. There exist a totally real field E of even degree over ℚ in which p splits completely and a regular algebraic cuspidal automorphic representation π of GL₂(𝔸_E) of weight 0 (parallel weight 2, trivial algebraic part) such that, for the attached p-adic Galois representation ρ_π : Gal_E → GL₂(ℚ̄_p) and its reduction ρ̄_π (after conjugation into GL₂(k_L)): (1) ρ_π is unramified outside p; (2) SL₂(k_L) ⊂ ρ̄_π(Gal_E) ⊂ GL₂(k_L), so ρ̄_π is absolutely irreducible; (3) ρ̄_π|_{Gal_{E_v}} ≅ r̄ for every place v | p (E_v = ℚ_p).
hypotheses: p odd: the only place in CDN where p > 2 is used.
[k_L : 𝔽_p] ≥ 2 (CDN take ≥ 3, after enlarging L), so that SL₂(k_L) is perfect and adequacy holds; this costs nothing since L may be enlarged.
proofSteps: Realise r̄ globally (Gee–Kisin Proposition A.1): by Calegari’s potential realisation of local Galois data (PotentialModularityAndCompatibleSystems R23.1/potential-global-galois-local-data) there are a totally real L⁺ with L⁺_v ≅ ℚ_p and a totally odd r̄′ : Gal_{L⁺} → GL₂(k_L) with image GL₂(k_L), r̄′|_{Gal_{L⁺_v}} ≅ r̄ at every v | p, unramified away from p after a solvable base change.

Make it modular (Gee–Kisin Theorem A.2): every local restriction at v | p has a potentially Barsotti–Tate lift (Snowden §7.8 when it is irreducible, Barnet-Lamb–Gee–Geraghty Lemma 6.1.6 when it is reducible; requested from LocalGaloisDeformationRings R08.6), so Snowden’s potential modularity theorem (R23.3/snowden-totally-real-potential-residual-modularity) gives a totally real Galois F⁺/L⁺ in which the places above p split completely, linearly disjoint from the field cut out by r̄′, and a weight-zero cuspidal π′ with ρ̄_{π′} ≅ r̄′|_{Gal_{F⁺}} and conductor potentially prime to p (Gee–Kisin Corollary A.3).

Remove ramification away from p and make the degree even by a further solvable totally real base change (GL2AutomorphicRepresentationsAndTransfer R17.4/solvable-base-change); cuspidality is preserved because no step meets the quadratic self-twist exception: π ≅ π ⊗ η with η quadratic would make ρ̄_π ≅ ρ̄_π ⊗ η̄, hence induced from a quadratic extension, with solvable projective image, impossible once the image contains SL₂(k_L) with |k_L| ≥ 4; SL₂(k_L) equals its commutator subgroup for |k_L| ≥ 4, so it stays in the image after abelian base changes (DPS Proposition 8.1).
The Galois representation attached to a parallel-weight-two Hilbert eigenform is AutomorphicGaloisRepresentations R19.2/all-cohomological-hilbert-representation.
acceptance: For r̄ irreducible, the global ρ̄_π is irreducible on each decomposition group above p.
For r̄ = r̄_{χ₁,χ₂} a non-split extension of characters, ρ̄_π is absolutely irreducible globally but reducible at every v | p.
[E : ℚ] is even, so a quaternion algebra over E ramified exactly at the infinite places exists (R17.3/invariant-exchange).

sources.match: For r̄ : Gal_{ℚ_p} → GL₂(k_L) there are a totally real E of even degree with p totally split and a regular algebraic cuspidal weight-0 representation of GL₂(𝔸_E) whose Galois representation is unramified outside p, has residual image between SL₂(k_L) and GL₂(k_L) and restricts to r̄ at every place above p; this is the only use of p > 2.
The globalisation with properties (1)–(4), deduced from Gee–Kisin Corollary A.3 by solvable base change and the perfectness of SL₂(𝔽).

sources.locator: Appendix A: Proposition A.1, Theorem A.2 and Corollary A.3, pp. 36–37
sources.match: Realising a local residual representation by a global one with prescribed local restrictions (via Calegari), and potential modularity in weight 0 with level potentially prime to p (via Snowden).

nodes.title: The definite quaternionic block module and the occurrence of every member of a block
nodes.statement: Let p > 2, r̄ : Gal_{ℚ_p} → GL₂(k_L), B the block of the locally finite category of smooth k_L[GL₂(ℚ_p)]-representations attached to r̄^{ss} (PadicLocalLanglandsForGL2Qp R30.5/blocks-classification), and (E, π, ρ = ρ_π) as in SZ.4/residual-globalisation, conjugated so that ρ(Gal_E) ⊂ GL₂(O_L). Put ψ = χ_cyc · det ρ, viewed as a character of 𝔸_f^×/E^× (uniformisers ↦ geometric Frobenius), fix 𝔭 | p and a real place ∞₀, ζ = ψ_𝔭. Let D₀/E be the quaternion algebra ramified exactly at the infinite places, D the algebra with invariants exchanged at 𝔭 and ∞₀ (R17.3/invariant-exchange), U^𝔭 = ∏_{v ∤ 𝔭∞} U_v with U_v = GL₂(O_{E_v}) except at an auxiliary place w₁ where U_{w₁} = {g ≡ (1 ∗; 0 1) mod ϖ_{w₁}}, w₁ chosen with N(w₁) prime to 2Np, N(w₁) ≢ 1 mod p and the ratio of the eigenvalues of ρ̄(Frob_{w₁}) not in {1, N(w₁)^{±1}} (N the product of the orders of the finite stabiliser groups of the double cosets), 𝔪 the residual maximal ideal of T^{univ}_S (T_v ↦ tr ρ̄(Frob_v), S_v ↦ N(v)⁻¹ det ρ̄(Frob_v)), and S_{ψ,λ,𝔪} = Hom_{U^𝔭_p}(λ, S_ψ(U^p, L/O_L))_𝔪 for a representation λ = ⊗_{v|p, v≠𝔭} λ_v with central characters ψ_v chosen so that S_{ψ,λ,𝔪} ≠ 0. Then: (1) w₁ exists; (2) S_{ψ,λ,𝔪} is a non-zero admissible object of Rep^ζ_B GL₂(ℚ_p) whose restriction to GL₂(ℤ_p) is injective in the category of smooth representations with central character ζ; (3) with A = R^{ps,ζ}_B the pseudo-deformation ring of the block acting on S_{ψ,λ,𝔪}, M_{ψ,λ,𝔪} := (k_L ⊗_A S^∨_{ψ,λ,𝔪})^∨ = S_{ψ,λ,𝔪}[𝔪_A] is of finite length in Rep^ζ_B GL₂(ℚ_p), and every π ∈ B is an irreducible subquotient of M_{ψ,λ,𝔪}.
hypotheses: p > 2; [k_L : 𝔽_p] ≥ 3 after enlarging L; ζ, ψ and the local types λ_v as in DPS Proposition 8.4 and Lemma 8.6.
The quaternion algebras, the level and the Hecke conventions are those of R17.3/invariant-exchange, R18.3/residual-hecke-ideal and R31.1/definite-quaternionic-completed-module.
proofSteps: (1) Chebotarev: choose g in the Galois group of the field cut out by ρ̄ and ζ_p with non-trivial image in Gal(E(ζ_p)/E) and eigenvalue ratio avoiding {1, N(w₁)^{±1}}; infinitely many w₁ have Frob_{w₁} conjugate to g (DPS Lemma 8.2).

(2) Non-vanishing, admissibility and injectivity over K_p = ∏_{v|p} GL₂(ℤ_p) of S_ψ(U^p, L/O_L)_𝔪 (DPS Proposition 8.4; CompletedCohomology R31.1/definite-quaternionic-tower-structure (c)–(d), whose smallness hypotheses hold at the level U thanks to w₁) and the choice of λ (DPS Lemma 8.6); taking Hom_{U^𝔭_p}(λ, −) of a K_p-injective module gives a GL₂(ℤ_p)-injective one at 𝔭, and the 𝔪-part lies in the block of r̄^{ss} (Paškūnas, consequences of Ludwig, Lemmas 5.1–5.3, Proposition 5.4). In PAS22 formula(26), use the lattice dual Hom_O(λ,O), as corrected by DPS23 footnote 15 (E6); the torsion Pontryagin dual would make the tensor formula wrong.

(3) Apply R30.6/block-occurrence once there is a non-zero characteristic-zero specialisation with absolutely irreducible local Galois representation. Follow PAS22 Theorem 6.5 and CDN23 Proposition 4.10: choose a small open pro-p V_𝔭 and a supercuspidal type, together with the algebraic weight and compatible central character, so that a Hecke eigenvector in Hom_{V_𝔭}(γ,S_{ψ,λ}(U^𝔭,O_L)_𝔪[1/p]) gives an automorphic representation supercuspidal at 𝔭 (R16.3/cdt-inertia-multiplicity). This Hom space is non-zero because the non-zero fixed-central-character injective S restricts to copies of C_ζ(V_𝔭,L/O_L); dually it is projective in the fixed-central-character compact category and, on a sufficiently small pro-p subgroup, free over the corresponding central-character quotient of O_L[[V_𝔭]]. It is not generally free over O_L[[V_𝔭]] itself. The space is finite-dimensional by admissibility, so it has a Hecke eigenvector after finite coefficient extension. The global residual representation is absolutely irreducible by SZ.4/residual-globalisation; this is the residual irreducibility required by R19.5/kisin-hilbert-coefficient-prime, even when the local residual r̄ is reducible. Local–global compatibility at p identifies the Weil–Deligne representation with that of the supercuspidal local factor; the associated two-dimensional p-adic Galois representation is then absolutely irreducible. R30.6 yields finite length and occurrence of every member of the block.
acceptance: For r̄ absolutely irreducible, B = {π̄} is a single supersingular representation and M_{ψ,λ,𝔪} is a successive extension of copies of π̄.
For r̄ = r̄_{χ₁,χ₂} with (χ₁, χ₂) generic, the irreducible subquotients of M_{ψ,λ,𝔪} are exactly I(χ₁, χ₂) and I(χ₂, χ₁).
M_{ψ,λ,𝔪} is killed by 𝔪_A, so A acts on it through k_L.

sources.match: The two quaternion algebras with invariants exchanged at 𝔭 and ∞₀, the tame level with the auxiliary place w₁ from DPS Lemma 8.2, the spaces S_ψ(U^p, A) and S_{ψ,λ}(U^𝔭, A), the universal Hecke algebra and the maximal ideal 𝔪 of ρ̄.

Non-vanishing, admissibility and injectivity of the localised spaces, S_{ψ,λ,𝔪} admissible in the block of r̄^{ss} and injective over K, finite length of M_{ψ,λ,𝔪} and occurrence of every member of the block, via Paškūnas–Tung and a supercuspidal type.
Existence of the auxiliary place w₁ by Chebotarev, admissibility and injectivity of S_ψ(U^p, L/O)_𝔪, and the choice of λ with non-zero λ-part.
The construction of a supercuspidal type on a pro-𝔭 subgroup whose Hecke eigenvectors are supercuspidal at 𝔭, used for the non-vanishing of a specialisation.
