sources.match: Provides the fixed-central-character injectivity and local block membership, and constructs the non-zero compatible-type Hom space using central-character regular functions.

nodes.title: Scholze’s functor on Hecke-torsion parts of quaternionic forms (Paškūnas)
nodes.statement: In the setting of SZ.4/global-block-occurrence, let Ĥ¹_{ψ,λ}(U^𝔭, −)_𝔪 be the ψ-isotypic, λ-typical, 𝔪-localised completed cohomology of the Shimura curves attached to D (CompletedCohomology R31.1/shimura-curve-completed-cohomology). For every ideal I of the Hecke algebra T(U^𝔭)_𝔪, the isomorphism S¹(S_{ψ,λ,𝔪}) ≅ Ĥ¹_{ψ,λ,𝔪} of R31.4/scholze-functor-and-completed-cohomology-of-shimura-curves induces an injection S¹(S_{ψ,λ,𝔪}[I]) ↪ Ĥ¹_{ψ,λ,𝔪}[I] on whose cokernel the reduced-norm-one units of O_{D_𝔭} act trivially; if r̄^{ss} is not of the form χ ⊕ χω, it is an isomorphism. In particular, if r̄ = r̄_{χ₁,χ₂} with (χ₁, χ₂) generic, S¹(M_{ψ,λ,𝔪}) ≅ Ĥ¹_{ψ,λ}(U^𝔭, k_L)_𝔪[𝔪_A], the ideal 𝔪_A acting through the Hecke algebra.
hypotheses: r̄^{ss} ≠ χ ⊕ χω for the isomorphism; the injection holds in general.

Paškūnas states the lemma for the λ-parts of S(U^p, L/O_L)_𝔪 without fixing the central character; the ψ-isotypic form here follows by applying it to ideals containing the ideal generated by the S_v − ψ(Frob_v) (as in his Lemma 6.2), or directly from the ψ-isotypic isomorphism of R31.4 by the argument below.
The global non-Eisenstein hypothesis, not local irreducibility of r̄, supplies S⁰(S)=0. The Hecke algebra is noetherian, so every ideal I has finitely many generators.
proofSteps: First S⁰(S)=0: the global residual representation is absolutely irreducible, so the non-Eisenstein localisation of degree-zero Shimura-curve cohomology vanishes; transport through the degree-zero geometric identification, and then take the ψ- and λ-parts. This is the input at the start of SCH18 Proposition 7.7 (p.29), retained in PAS22 Lemma 6.1. For I=(f₁,…,f_r), write Q=S/S[I], which embeds in S^r via the f_i, and C=coker(Q→S^r). Since S⁰ is left exact, S⁰(Q)=0; the first long exact sequence gives S¹(S[I]) ↪ S¹(S). Its image lies in S¹(S)[I]. The discrepancy inside the latter injects into ker(S¹(Q)→S¹(S^r)), a quotient of S⁰(C); norm-one units act trivially on this by SZ.1/scholze-galois-and-degree-zero. Apply the Hecke-equivariant R31.4 isomorphism to obtain the stated injection and cokernel control. S⁰(S)=0 cannot be omitted.

If the map is not surjective, some subquotient of S_ψ(U^p, L/O_L)_𝔪 has non-zero SL₂(ℚ_p)-invariants, so the block of r̄^{ss} contains a character; by the block classification (R30.5/blocks-classification) this forces r̄^{ss} ≅ χ ⊕ χω.
For r̄ = r̄_{χ₁,χ₂} generic, take I generated by 𝔪_A; then S_{ψ,λ,𝔪}[𝔪_A] = M_{ψ,λ,𝔪} and Ĥ¹_{ψ,λ,𝔪}[𝔪_A] = Ĥ¹_{ψ,λ}(U^𝔭, k_L)_𝔪[𝔪_A] (CDN §4.1.5).
acceptance: For I = 0 the lemma is the isomorphism of R31.4 (1).
For r̄^{ss} = χ ⊕ χω the cokernel may be non-zero and is a representation of D_𝔭^× trivial on the norm-one units.
The comparison is compatible with Gal_{ℚ_p} × D_𝔭^× and with the Hecke action.

sources.match: S¹ of the I-torsion of the λ-part of quaternionic forms injects into the I-torsion of completed cohomology, with cokernel killed by the norm-one units of O_{D_𝔭}, and is an isomorphism unless r̄^{ss} ≅ χ ⊕ χω.
The isomorphism S¹(S_{ψ,λ}(U^p, L/O)_𝔪) ≅ Ĥ¹_{ψ,λ}(U^p, L/O)_𝔪 of T(U^p)_𝔪[G_{ℚ_p} × D_p^×]-modules.
Combines Proposition 4.11 and Paškūnas’s Lemma 6.1 to identify S¹(M) with Ĥ¹_{ψ,λ}(U^𝔭, k_L)_𝔪[𝔪_A].

nodes.title: Galois invariants of S¹ of generic principal series (CDN Proposition 4.3)
nodes.statement: Let p > 2 and (χ₁, χ₂) a generic pair of smooth characters ℚ_p^× → 𝔽̄_p^× (χ₁χ₂⁻¹ ≠ 1, ε^{±1}, ε the reduction of x ↦ x|x|), viewed also as characters of Gal_{ℚ_p} by local class field theory, and let I(χ₁, χ₂) = Ind_B^G(χ₂ ⊗ χ₁ε⁻¹). If K/ℚ_p is finite and S¹(I(χ₁, χ₂))^{Gal_K} ≠ 0, then χ₁|_{Gal_K}=1 or χ₂|_{Gal_K}=1. Equivalently, the finite abelian extension fixed by ker χ₁ or by ker χ₂ is contained in K; K need not be Galois over ℚ_p.
hypotheses: p > 2 (through SZ.4/residual-globalisation); characters defined over k_L after enlarging L, the representations regarded over k_L as in CDN §1.3.2.
proofSteps: Let r̄ = r̄_{χ₁,χ₂} be the non-split extension 0 → χ₁ → r̄ → χ₂ → 0, the residual representation of the block {I(χ₁, χ₂), I(χ₂, χ₁)}; globalise it (SZ.4/residual-globalisation) and form M = M_{ψ,λ,𝔪}, of finite length with irreducible subquotients exactly I(χ₁, χ₂) and I(χ₂, χ₁) (SZ.4/global-block-occurrence).

S² vanishes on both principal series (SZ.3/ludwig-vanishing (a)) and S⁰ vanishes on both (no SL₂(ℚ_p)-invariants, SZ.1/scholze-galois-and-degree-zero (b)), so the long exact sequences make S¹(M) a successive extension of copies of S¹(I(χ₁, χ₂)) and S¹(I(χ₂, χ₁)); in particular S¹(I(χ₁, χ₂)) is a Gal_{ℚ_p}-subquotient of S¹(M).

S¹(M) ≅ Ĥ¹_{ψ,λ}(U^𝔭, k_L)_𝔪[𝔪_A] (SZ.4/hecke-torsion-comparison), and by Carayol–Scholze isotypy (R31.4/scholze-functor-and-completed-cohomology-of-shimura-curves (2)) and ρ̄_π|_{Gal_{E_𝔭}} ≅ r̄ this is r̄ ⊗ N′ with Gal_{ℚ_p} acting trivially on N′.

Every subquotient W of r̄ ⊗ N′ has a two-step filtration with graded pieces subquotients of χ₁ ⊗ N′ and χ₂ ⊗ N′, both direct sums of copies of χ₁, resp. χ₂; a non-zero Gal_K-invariant vector of W has non-zero Gal_K-invariant image in one graded piece, so χ₁ or χ₂ is trivial on Gal_K.
acceptance: For fixed K and a fixed central character δ, only finitely many generic pairs with χ₁χ₂ε⁻¹ = δ can have S¹(I(χ₁, χ₂))^{Gal_K} ≠ 0, because only finitely many smooth characters of ℚ_p^× are trivial on the norm group N_{K/ℚ_p}(K^×); this finiteness is what SZ.5 uses.
For K = ℚ_p the conclusion says χ₁ or χ₂ is trivial.

Under simultaneous twist by η, replace S¹(I) by S¹(I)⊗(η⁻¹⊠η) and the characters by χ₁η,χ₂η. The invariant-space hypothesis must be twisted as well; invariants under Gal_K need not be unchanged unless η|_{Gal_K}=1.
A pair with χ₁=χ₂, χ₁χ₂⁻¹=ε, or χ₁χ₂⁻¹=ε⁻¹ fails genericity; simultaneous twisting and swapping the characters preserve genericity.
For non-Galois K the conclusion is still the restriction-to-Gal_K statement, with no use of a quotient Gal(K/ℚ_p).

sources.match: If S¹(I(χ₁, χ₂))^{𝒢_K} ≠ 0 for a generic pair, then χ₁ or χ₂ factors through Gal(K/ℚ_p); Hellmann–Wang treat finer structure of S¹(I(χ₁, χ₂)).
The proof: Ludwig’s vanishing, vanishing of S⁰, Proposition 4.11 with Paškūnas’s Lemma 6.1, and isotypy (Proposition 4.12) showing that S¹(I(χ₁, χ₂)) is a subquotient of r̄ ⊗ N′.
Genericity of a pair of characters, the representations I(χ₁, χ₂), I(χ₂, χ₁), their unique non-split extension and V(I(χ₁, χ₂)) = χ₁, V(I(χ₂, χ₁)) = χ₂, V(Π_{χ₁,χ₂}) = r̄_{χ₁,χ₂}.

nodes.title: Functors of finite image on irreducible representations
nodes.statement: Let G′ = GL₂(ℚ_p)/p^ℤ and k_L a finite field of characteristic p. A function V assigning to every isomorphism class of smooth irreducible k_L[G′]-modules π a k_L-vector space V(π) is of finite image if V(π) is finite-dimensional for every π and V(π) = 0 for all but finitely many π. For functors defined on all smooth k_L[G′]-modules the condition is imposed on the irreducible ones.
hypotheses: Only irreducible π are tested; no condition is imposed on reducible arguments.
proofSteps: Define the predicate on families of arbitrary k_L-vector spaces indexed by isomorphism classes of irreducibles: each value must be finite-dimensional and the support must be finite. Finite-dimensionality is a condition, not an assumed codomain restriction.
Stability under subobjects and extensions is checked pointwise: dimensions add along exact sequences and supports are contained in unions.

For the cohomology API, support cannot increase. Compact Lie finiteness is SZ.0/compact-lie-admissible-cohomology. In the Weil case, a finite action or 1-cocycle gives a homomorphism to a finite group (use V⋊Aut(V) for a cocycle); its inertia kernel is open and stable under a Frobenius power, so it factors through a finite Galois quotient. Thus H⁰/H¹(W_K,V) agree with H⁰/H¹(Gal_K,V), finite by ClassFieldTheory Layer 5. Compactness of W_K is neither assumed nor true.
acceptance: The zero functor is of finite image.
π ↦ Hom_{G′}(V, π) for V of finite length is of finite image.
π ↦ π^{I₁} (pro-p Iwahori invariants) is not of finite image: it is non-zero on every π.

sources.match: A functor π ↦ V(π) to k_L-modules is said to be of finite image if V(π) is finite-dimensional for every smooth irreducible k_L[G′]-module π and zero for almost every π.

For W_K with K/ℚ_p finite the same holds in degrees 0 and 1: finite actions and finite-valued continuous 1-cocycles extend to Gal_K, so use ClassFieldTheory Layer 5 finite_H and Layer 9’s inertia/Weil topology.

nodes.title: Ascent from the arithmetic Drinfeld levels to infinite level (CDN Lemmas 4.13 and 4.17)
nodes.statement: Let F = ℚ_p with p > 2, ϖ = p, G = GL₂(ℚ_p), G′ = G/p^ℤ, Ǧ = D^× and Ǧ₀ = O_D^× and Ǧ_n = 1 + 𝔪_D^n for n ≥ 1, K/ℚ_p finite, M^p_{n,K} the arithmetic level-n Drinfeld space (ET.6a/rank-two-arithmetic-descent), M^p_{Dr,∞} = M_{Dr,∞,ℂ_p}/p^ℤ and M_∞ = M_{LT,∞,ℂ_p} ≅ M_{Dr,∞,ℂ_p} (ET.6a/el-duality). (a) There are strictly exact sequences of prodiscrete G′-modules 0 → H¹(Gal_K, H⁰_ét(M^p_{n,ℂ_p}, k_L)) → H¹_ét(M^p_{n,K}, k_L) → H¹_ét(M^p_{n,ℂ_p}, k_L)^{Gal_K} and 0 → H¹(Ǧ_n, H⁰_ét(M^p_{Dr,∞}, k_L)) → H¹_ét(M^p_{n,ℂ_p}, k_L) → H¹_ét(M^p_{Dr,∞}, k_L)^{Ǧ_n}, with H⁰_ét(M^p_{Dr,∞}, k_L) ≅ C⁰(ℚ_p^×/p^{2ℤ}, k_L) and H^i(Ǧ_n, C⁰(ℚ_p^×/p^{2ℤ}, k_L)) finite-dimensional; and H¹_ét(M^p_{Dr,∞}, k_L) ≅ H¹_ét(M_{Dr,∞}, k_L)^{p^ℤ}. (b) Consequently the functor π ↦ Hom^cont_{k_L[G′]}(π^∨, H¹_ét(M^p_{n,K}, k_L)) is of finite image (SZ.5/finite-image-functor) as soon as π ↦ Y(π) := Hom^cont_{k_L[G]}(π^∨, H¹_ét(M_∞, k_L))^{W_K × Ǧ_n} is. (c) Y is of finite image as soon as π ↦ S¹(π)^{Gal_K × Ǧ_n} is. (d) For any finite F/ℚ_p (no descent to F, no p^ℤ-quotient), the same arguments give an exact sequence 0 → H¹(Ǧ_n, C⁰(F^×, k_L)) → H¹_ét(M_{n,ℂ_p}, k_L) → H¹_ét(M_∞, k_L)^{Ǧ_n}.
hypotheses: F = ℚ_p, p > 2 in (a)–(c); (d) for every finite F/ℚ_p.
Prodiscrete topologies come from Stein covers; the Weil and Galois invariants of S¹(π) agree by SZ.1/scholze-galois-and-degree-zero (a).
proofSteps: (a), first sequence: on a Stein cover {V_s} of M^p_{n,K}, the Hochschild–Serre spectral sequences for V_{s,ℂ_p}/V_s (de Jong–van der Put, étale cohomology of rigid spaces) give exact sequences of discrete modules; the first term does not depend on s (finitely many components), so it is Mittag-Leffler and the limit sequence is strictly exact (as in the proof of CDN Theorem 2.1, step 3).

(a), second sequence: the Cartan–Leray spectral sequence of the pro-étale Ǧ_n-torsor M^p_{Dr,∞} → M^p_{n,ℂ_p}, built exactly as in SZ.2/cartan-leray-spectral-sequence; π₀(M_{Dr,∞}) ≅ ℚ_p^× with Ǧ acting through Nrd and p acting through det = p² (SZ.0/lubin-tate-components (c)) gives H⁰ = C⁰(ℚ_p^×/p^{2ℤ}, k_L), an admissible Ǧ_n-module, whose Ǧ_n-cohomology is finite (SZ.0/compact-lie-admissible-cohomology (b)). M^p_{Dr,∞} is the union of the height-zero and height-one parts of M_{Dr,∞}, so a Stein perfectoid exhaustion and its Mittag-Leffler property (ET.6a/stein-mittag-leffler) restrict to it.

(a), last identification: the étale p^ℤ-torsor M_{Dr,∞} → M^p_{Dr,∞} gives 0 → H¹(p^ℤ, H⁰) → H¹(M^p_{Dr,∞}) → H⁰(p^ℤ, H¹(M_{Dr,∞})) → 0 and H¹(p^ℤ, C⁰(ℚ_p^×, k_L)) = H¹(p^ℤ, Ind_1^{p^ℤ} C⁰(ℤ_p^× ⊔ pℤ_p^×, k_L)) = 0 by Shapiro (SZ.2/fust-cohomology (b)); the source writes C⁰(ℤ_p^×, k_L) here (source issue E3), which does not change the vanishing.

(b) Apply Hom^cont_{k_L[G′]}(π^∨, −) and Gal_K-, Ǧ_n-invariants to the sequences of (a); the outer terms give functors of finite image because M^p_{n,ℂ_p} has finitely many components and H^i(Ǧ_n, C⁰(ℚ_p^×/p^{2ℤ}, k_L)) is finite (CDN Lemma 4.13); transport M_{Dr,∞} to M_∞ by duality.

(c) Use the exact sequence 0 → V₁(π) → S¹(π) → Hom^cont_{k_L[G]}(π^∨, H¹_ét(M_∞, k_L)) → V₂(π) of SZ.2/comparison-map, where V₁, V₂ are of finite image (finite-dimensional, and zero outside the finitely many twists of the Steinberg block with given central character, SZ.2/fust-cohomology (d)); the cohomology of W_K × Ǧ_n with values in V₁(π) is of finite image, so the invariants of the cokernel of V₁ → S¹ and then Y(π) are of finite image (CDN Lemma 4.17). The required H⁰/H¹ finiteness for W_K is the finite-module comparison with Gal_K in SZ.5/finite-image-functor, using ClassFieldTheory Layers 5 and 9; for W_K × Ǧ_n use the Hochschild–Serre sequence and compact Lie finiteness.
(d) Steps 1–3 are geometric and do not use F = ℚ_p (CDN, proof of Theorem 4.22).
acceptance: For n = 0, Ǧ_0 = O_D^× and C⁰(ℚ_p^×/p^{2ℤ}, k_L) restricted to O_D^× is, through Nrd, two copies of C⁰(ℤ_p^×, k_L) (ℚ_p^×/p^{2ℤ} = ℤ_p^× ⊔ pℤ_p^×), whose cohomology is finite.
If π is not of the form I(χ₁, χ₂) and not in a Steinberg twist, the reduction in (c) is an equality Y(π) = S¹(π)^{W_K × Ǧ_n}.
Applied to π with Hom^cont(π^∨, H¹_ét(M^p_{n,K}, k_L)) ≠ 0, (b) and (c) produce a non-zero class in S¹(π)^{Gal_K × Ǧ_n} up to finitely many exceptions.

sources.match: Three-step ascent from M^p_{n,K} to M^p_{n,ℂ_p}, to M^p_{Dr,∞} and to M_{Dr,∞}, with the strictly exact sequences (4.14), (4.16), the identification (4.15) of H⁰ (printed with ℚ_p^×/p^ℤ; corrected to ℚ_p^×/p^{2ℤ}, source issue E3) and the vanishing of H¹(p^ℤ, C⁰(ℚ_p^×, k_L)) by Shapiro.
If π ↦ S¹(π)^{𝒢_K × Ǧ_n} is of finite image then so is π ↦ Y(π), through the sequence (4.18).
The geometric steps give 0 → H¹(Ǧ_n, C⁰(F^×, k_L)) → H¹_ét(M_{n,ℂ_p}, k_L) → H¹_ét(M_∞, k_L)^{Ǧ_n} for every F.

nodes.title: Vanishing of multiplicities for almost every irreducible (CDN Theorem 0.9)
nodes.statement: Let F = ℚ_p with p > 2, ϖ = p, n ≥ 0 and K/ℚ_p finite. For every smooth irreducible k_L[G′]-module π, Hom^cont_{k_L[G′]}(π^∨, H¹_ét(M^p_{n,K}, k_L)) is finite-dimensional over k_L, and it vanishes for all but finitely many isomorphism classes of such π; that is, the functor is of finite image.
hypotheses: F = ℚ_p and p > 2; the statement is specific to ℚ_p (CDN Theorem 2.13 gives non-admissibility phenomena for F ≠ ℚ_p).
proofSteps: By MP.1/central-ext (CDN Lemma 1.22), the centre of G′ acts through ℤ_p^×/(1+pℤ_p) ≅ 𝔽_p^×: p acts trivially by the quotient, and the central pro-p subgroup acts trivially on every smooth irreducible in characteristic p. Its characters are the p−1 characters into 𝔽_p^× ⊂ k_L^×, so there are finitely many possible central characters. Fix one, δ. Admissibility of each π is R30.2/modp-irreducibles.
By SZ.5/drinfeld-tower-ascent (b)–(c) it suffices that π ↦ S¹(π)^{Gal_K × Ǧ_n} is of finite image. Finite-dimensionality: S¹(π) is an admissible Ǧ-module (SZ.1/scholze-finiteness).

Finiteness of the support: put π̄ = 𝔽̄_p ⊗_{k_L} π; then S¹(π̄) ≅ 𝔽̄_p ⊗_{k_L} S¹(π) (SZ.1/scholze-functor, base change, as ℙ¹_{ℂ_p} is quasicompact). Let T be the set of irreducible 𝔽̄_p[G′]-modules τ with S¹(τ)^{Gal_K} ≠ 0. By the classification only finitely many τ with given central character are not generic principal series (Remark 1.9, R30.2/modp-irreducibles), and among generic principal series only finitely many have S¹(τ)^{Gal_K} ≠ 0 by SZ.4/key-local-proposition; so T is finite.

If π has S¹(π)^{Gal_K × Ǧ_n} ≠ 0 then π̄ has a constituent in T; π̄ is semisimple with pairwise distinct Galois-conjugate constituents (MP.0/scalar-extension, Lemma 1.7), and Hom commutes with field extension (Lemma 1.6), so two non-isomorphic such π cannot share a constituent; hence only finitely many π occur.
acceptance: For K = ℚ_p only finitely many π with S¹(π)^{Gal_{ℚ_p} × Ǧ_n} ≠ 0 occur, by the same proof.
The finitely many exceptional π include the irreducible constituents of the cosocle of H¹_ét(M^p_{n,K}, k_L)^∨ (SZ.5/finite-length).
Twisting by characters of ℚ_p^×/p^{2ℤ} that are trivial on N_{K/ℚ_p}(K^×) preserves the finite set of exceptions up to the twist.

sources.match: For [K : ℚ_p] < ∞, Hom^cont_{k_L[G′]}(π^∨, H¹_ét(M^p_{n,K}, k_L)) = 0 for all but finitely many smooth irreducible π.
Finite-dimensionality from Scholze’s finiteness and finiteness of the support from (4.19), Remarque 1.9, Proposition 4.3 and Lemmas 1.6–1.7.

nodes.title: Finite length of the mod p cohomology of the Drinfeld tower (CDN Theorem 4.1)
nodes.statement: Let F = ℚ_p with p > 2, ϖ = p, n ≥ 0 and K/ℚ_p finite. (a) H¹_ét(M^p_{n,K}, k_L) is the Pontryagin dual of a smooth k_L[G′]-representation of finite length; in particular this representation is admissible and finitely presented, and H¹_ét(M^p_{n,K}, μ_p)^∨ is a smooth admissible G-representation of finite length as a ℤ_p[G]-module. (b) For every k ≥ 1, H¹_ét(M^p_{n,K}, O_L/ϖ_L^k)^∨ is a smooth admissible G′-representation of finite length. (c) For every smooth admissible k_L[G′]-module π with a central character, Hom^cont_{k_L[G′]}(π^∨, H¹_ét(M^p_{n,ℂ_p}, k_L)) is finite-dimensional.
hypotheses: F = ℚ_p, p > 2.
Finite presentation of the dual (CDN Theorem 2.1) is an input from the pending pro-étale cohomology design; it is recorded as a gap.

In (c) CDN state the corollary for every smooth admissible π; the argument through SZ.2/fust-cohomology (e) is recorded for π with a central character, which covers every irreducible π (MP.1/central-ext) and the representations of SZ.6.
proofSteps: Reduce to K large: M^p_{n,K} has finitely many components, so H⁰_ét(M^p_{n,K′}, k_L) is finite for K′/K finite and the Hochschild–Serre spectral sequence for Gal(K′/K) passes the statement from K′ to K.

For K large, V := H¹_ét(M^p_{n,K}, k_L)^∨ is a smooth finitely presented, in particular finite type, G′-module (CDN Theorem 2.1, gap ScholzeFunctorAndModpCohomologyOfTheLubinTateTower/gap/proetale-finite-presentation).

By the cosocle criterion (ModpRepresentations MP.1/cosocle-length, Theorem 1.21) V has finite length once its cosocle does, i.e. once π ↦ Hom_{k_L[G′]}(V, π) ≅ Hom^cont_{k_L[G′]}(π^∨, H¹_ét(M^p_{n,K}, k_L)) is of finite image (SZ.5/finite-image-functor, cosocle_iff), which is SZ.5/almost-all-vanishing.

Admissibility and finite presentation follow from finite length for GL₂(ℚ_p): irreducibles are admissible (R30.2/modp-irreducibles), admissible modules form a Serre subcategory (SZ.0/compact-lie-admissible-cohomology (a)), and finite type implies finite presentation over ℚ_p (ModpRepresentations MP.1/finite-type-presentation) (Remarque 0.13 (i)).
(b) Dévissage on k using Theorem 2.1 for O_L/ϖ_L^k (CDN Remarque 4.2).

(c) The proof of SZ.5/almost-all-vanishing with M^p_{n,ℂ_p} in place of M^p_{n,K} uses the Galois action only for the vanishing, not for finite-dimensionality (CDN Remarque 4.20, Corollaire 4.21); the needed finiteness of H^i(SL₂(ℚ_p), π) holds for admissible π with a central character (SZ.2/fust-cohomology (c), (e)).
acceptance: H¹_ét(M^p_{n,K}, k_L)^∨ has only finitely many irreducible constituents, each admissible and finitely presented.
For n = 0, M^p_{0,K} is the quotient of ℤ × Ω_{Dr} by p^ℤ, and the theorem gives finite length of the dual of the mod p cohomology of two copies of the Drinfeld half-plane over K.
Taking π = the trivial character in (c), Hom^cont_{G′}(1, H¹_ét(M^p_{n,ℂ_p}, k_L)) is finite-dimensional.

sources.locator: Théorème 4.1, p. 37 (= Théorème 0.2, p. 3), with Remarque 4.2
sources.match: For every finite K/ℚ_p the G-module H¹_ét(M^p_{n,K}, k_L) is the dual of a smooth representation of finite length; the O_L/ϖ_L^k-version follows with Theorem 2.1, giving admissibility of the duals.
Reduction to K large, finite presentation by Theorem 2.1, the cosocle criterion Theorem 1.21, and the finite image of π ↦ Hom^cont_{k_L[G′]}(π^∨, H¹_ét(M^p_{n,K}, k_L)).

sources.locator: Remarque 4.20 and Corollaire 4.21, p. 46; Corollaire 0.12 (i) and Remarque 0.13 (i), p. 6
sources.match: Finite-dimensionality of multiplicities over ℂ_p, and finite length implying admissibility and finite presentation for GL₂(ℚ_p).

nodes.title: Finite-dimensionality of mod p multiplicities for every F (CDN Theorem 4.22)
nodes.statement: Let F/ℚ_p be finite, n ≥ 0, G = GL₂(F) and π a smooth admissible k_L-representation of G with a central character. Then Hom^cont_{k_L[G]}(π^∨, H¹_ét(M_{n,ℂ_p}, k_L)) is finite-dimensional over k_L, M_{n,ℂ_p} the level-n Drinfeld space over ℂ_p (no quotient by ϖ^ℤ).
hypotheses: F arbitrary finite over ℚ_p; π admissible with a central character (hence admissible for SL₂(F)).
proofSteps: By SZ.2/comparison-map (a) there is an exact sequence 0 → H¹(SL₂(F), π) → S¹(π) → Hom^cont_{k_L[G]}(π^∨, H¹_ét(M_∞, k_L)) → H²(SL₂(F), π), whose outer terms are finite-dimensional (SZ.2/fust-cohomology (c), (e)).
S¹(π) is an admissible Ǧ-module (SZ.1/scholze-finiteness), so Hom^cont_{k_L[G]}(π^∨, H¹_ét(M_∞, k_L))^{Ǧ_n} is finite-dimensional.

Apply Hom^cont_{k_L[G]}(π^∨, −) to 0 → H¹(Ǧ_n, C⁰(F^×, k_L)) → H¹_ét(M_{n,ℂ_p}, k_L) → H¹_ét(M_∞, k_L)^{Ǧ_n} (SZ.5/drinfeld-tower-ascent (d)); it remains to bound the first term. W = H¹(Ǧ_n, C⁰(O_F^×, k_L)) is finite-dimensional (SZ.0/compact-lie-admissible-cohomology (b)) and H¹(Ǧ_n, C⁰(F^×, k_L)) = Ind_1^{ϖ^ℤ} W, so Hom^cont_{k_L[G]}(π^∨, Ind_1^{ϖ^ℤ} W) injects into (π ⊗_{k_L} W)^{SL₂(F)}, finite-dimensional by admissibility of π over SL₂(F).
acceptance: For π a character δ∘det, the statement bounds the δ-isotypic G-invariant part of H¹_ét(M_{n,ℂ_p}, k_L).
For F = ℚ_p it contains SZ.5/finite-length (c) after passing to the quotient by p^ℤ.
For F ≠ ℚ_p the statement holds although the cohomology over a finite K is dual to non-admissible representations (CDN Theorem 2.13).

sources.locator: Théorème 4.22 with proof, p. 46 (= Théorème 0.7, p. 5)
sources.match: For π a smooth admissible k_L-representation of GL₂(F) with a central character, Hom^cont_{k_L[G]}(π^∨, H¹_ét(M_{n,ℂ_p}, k_L)) is finite-dimensional, via the general-F version of (3.14), Fust’s finiteness, Scholze’s admissibility and the geometric steps of Lemma 4.13.
For F = ℚ_p this is a mod p analogue of Theorem 0.16; over a finite K it would follow from Theorem 0.5, but not over ℂ_p.

nodes.title: The geometric multiplicity Π^geo_n(ρ̄) of a residual Galois representation
nodes.statement: Let F = ℚ_p, ϖ = p, n ≥ 0 and ρ̄ : Gal_{ℚ_p} → GL_d(k_L) a continuous representation on a finite-dimensional k_L-vector space. Define Π^geo_n(ρ̄) := Hom_{k_L[Gal_{ℚ_p}]}(ρ̄, H¹_ét(M^p_{n,ℂ_p}, k_L))^∨, the continuous k_L-linear dual of the space of Galois-equivariant maps from ρ̄ to the first étale cohomology of the level-n Drinfeld space over ℂ_p, with the G′-action induced by the action on the cohomology. More generally, for F/ℚ_p finite and ρ̄ : Gal_F → GL_d(k_L), Π^geo_n(ρ̄) := Hom_{k_L[Gal_F]}(ρ̄, H¹_ét(M^ϖ_{n,ℂ_p}, k_L))^∨.
hypotheses: The dual is taken with the topology for which Hom(ρ̄, H¹) is prodiscrete; Π^geo_n(ρ̄) is a smooth G′-module (CDN Corollary 2.12, Theorem 4.23 (a)).
proofSteps: The Galois-equivariant maps form a closed G′-stable subspace of Hom_{k_L}(ρ̄, H¹_ét(M^p_{n,ℂ_p}, k_L)) ≅ ρ̄^∨ ⊗ H¹; take its continuous dual.

If ρ̄ factors through a finite quotient H = Gal(F′/ℚ_p), Hom_{Gal}(ρ̄, H¹) = Hom_H(ρ̄, H¹(M^p_{n,ℂ_p}, k_L)^{Gal_{F′}}); if H¹(M^p_{n,ℂ_p}, k_L)^{Gal_{F′}} ≅ π^∨ then Hom_H(ρ̄, π^∨) ≅ (ρ̄^∨ ⊗ π^∨)^H ≅ ((ρ̄ ⊗ π)_H)^∨, so Π^geo_n(ρ̄) ≅ (ρ̄ ⊗_{k_L} π)_H, the H-coinvariants (CDN proof of Corollary 2.12).

For the smoothness assertion and general-F finite presentation, apply CDN Corollary 2.12: the Stein-cover Hochschild–Serre sequences compare H¹(M^ϖ_{n,ℂ_p},k_L)^{Gal_{F′}} with arithmetic H¹, with finite-dimensional outer terms by ClassFieldTheory Layer 5. Arithmetic finite presentation is the recorded proetale-finite-presentation gap. Then use MP.0/finite-presentation for finite sums, cokernels and finite-group coinvariants. This dependence is direct and does not follow merely from SZ.5 ascent. Keep the continuous dual on both sides of the initial Hom identification in the proof of CDN Corollary 2.12; its missing dual is the harmless misprint E5.
acceptance: Π^geo_n(ρ̄₁ ⊕ ρ̄₂) = Π^geo_n(ρ̄₁) ⊕ Π^geo_n(ρ̄₂).
For a character χ, Π^geo_n(χ) is the dual of the χ-isotypic Galois-invariant part (H¹ ⊗ χ⁻¹)^{Gal_{ℚ_p}}.

sources.match: Π^geo_n(ρ̄) is the dual of the space of Gal_{ℚ_p}-equivariant maps from ρ̄ to H¹_ét(M^p_{n,ℂ_p}, k_L).

For general F, the dual of Hom_{Gal_F}(ρ̄, H¹_ét(M^ϖ_{n,ℂ_p}, k_L)) is smooth of finite presentation, computed through a finite Galois F′ trivialising ρ̄ and the Hochschild–Serre sequences of a Stein cover.

uses.how: finite length, vanishing for absolutely irreducible ρ̄ of dimension > 2, and the block statement for d = 2
for F ≠ ℚ_p, Π^geo_n(ρ̄) can be non-admissible, a phenomenon absent ℓ-adically
the expected relation with the Breuil–Paškūnas representations for F unramified, recorded as an expectation

api.name: TauCetiRoadmap.ScholzeFunctor.geometricMultiplicity
api.statement: Π^geo_n(ρ̄) = Hom_{k_L[Gal_F]}(ρ̄, H¹_ét(M^ϖ_{n,ℂ_p}, k_L))^∨ with its G′-action.

api.name: TauCetiRoadmap.ScholzeFunctor.geometricMultiplicity_map
api.statement: A Galois-equivariant map ρ̄₁ → ρ̄₂ induces Π^geo_n(ρ̄₁) → Π^geo_n(ρ̄₂), compatibly with composition and identities.

api.name: TauCetiRoadmap.ScholzeFunctor.geometricMultiplicity_directSum
api.statement: Π^geo_n(ρ̄₁ ⊕ ρ̄₂) ≅ Π^geo_n(ρ̄₁) ⊕ Π^geo_n(ρ̄₂).

api.name: TauCetiRoadmap.ScholzeFunctor.geometricMultiplicity_rightExact
api.statement: A surjection ρ̄ ↠ ρ̄″ induces a surjection Π^geo_n(ρ̄) ↠ Π^geo_n(ρ̄″); exact sequences 0 → ρ̄′ → ρ̄ → ρ̄″ → 0 give right-exact sequences Π^geo_n(ρ̄′) → Π^geo_n(ρ̄) → Π^geo_n(ρ̄″) → 0.

api.name: TauCetiRoadmap.ScholzeFunctor.geometricMultiplicity_finiteQuotient
api.statement: If ρ̄ factors through H = Gal(F′/F) and H¹_ét(M^ϖ_{n,ℂ_p}, k_L)^{Gal_{F′}} ≅ π^∨ for a smooth G′-module π, then Π^geo_n(ρ̄) ≅ (ρ̄ ⊗_{k_L} π)_H, the H-coinvariants, as G′-modules.

api.name: TauCetiRoadmap.ScholzeFunctor.geometricMultiplicity_smooth
api.statement: For every finite F/ℚ_p, Π^geo_n(ρ̄) is a smooth finitely presented G′-module, by CDN Corollary 2.12 and the recorded arithmetic finite-presentation gap. For F=ℚ_p and p>2 it has finite length by SZ.6/geometric-multiplicity-theorem.

api.name: TauCetiRoadmap.ScholzeFunctor.geometricMultiplicity_level
api.statement: For m≥n, pullback along M^ϖ_m → M^ϖ_n induces Π^geo_m(ρ̄) → Π^geo_n(ρ̄), respecting identities, composition, and the maps in ρ̄. The dual topology is the continuous dual of the closed Galois-equivariant Hom space.

api.name: TauCetiRoadmap.ScholzeFunctor.geometricMultiplicity_ext
api.statement: Two elements of Π^geo_n(ρ̄) agree iff their values agree on every Galois-equivariant map ρ̄ → H¹_ét(M^ϖ_{n,ℂ_p},k_L). This identifies the underlying representation with the continuous dual, not the algebraic dual of an infinite prodiscrete space.

tests.name: TauCetiRoadmap.ScholzeFunctor.geometricMultiplicity_sum
tests.statement: For ρ̄ = χ₁ ⊕ χ₂, Π^geo_n(ρ̄) ≅ Π^geo_n(χ₁) ⊕ Π^geo_n(χ₂).

tests.name: TauCetiRoadmap.ScholzeFunctor.geometricMultiplicity_character
tests.statement: For a character χ : Gal_{ℚ_p} → k_L^×, Π^geo_n(χ) is the dual of (H¹_ét(M^p_{n,ℂ_p}, k_L) ⊗ χ⁻¹)^{Gal_{ℚ_p}}.

tests.name: TauCetiRoadmap.ScholzeFunctor.geometricMultiplicity_not_block
tests.statement: For the non-split r̄ = r̄_{χ₁,χ₂}, Π^geo_n(r̄) surjects onto Π^geo_n(χ₂) (maps factoring through the quotient χ₂), so Π^geo_n(r̄) need not lie in the block cut out by r̄ (CDN Remarque 4.25).

nodes.title: Finite length and vanishing of geometric multiplicities (CDN Theorem 4.23)
nodes.statement: Let F = ℚ_p with p > 2, n ≥ 0 and ρ̄ : Gal_{ℚ_p} → GL_d(k_L) continuous. (a) Π^geo_n(ρ̄) is a smooth G-module of finite length. (b) If d > 2 and ρ̄ is absolutely irreducible, Π^geo_n(ρ̄) = 0. (c) If d = 2 and ρ̄ is absolutely irreducible, Π^geo_n(ρ̄) is a successive extension of copies of Π(ρ̄), the supersingular representation attached to ρ̄ by the mod p local Langlands correspondence (the normalisation of the block bijection B ↔ ρ̄_B). Along the way: (d) (Lemma 4.24) in the setting of SZ.4/global-block-occurrence with r̄ = χ₁ ⊕ χ₂ reducible, for every G-submodule Z of M = M_{ψ,λ,𝔪} and compact open H ⊂ D^×, S¹(Z)^H and H¹(H, S¹(Z)) are finite-dimensional Gal_{ℚ_p}-representations all of whose irreducible subquotients are one-dimensional.
hypotheses: p > 2 and F = ℚ_p; in (c) the source proves the supersingular case of (b) in detail and indicates (c) in Remarque 4.25; the argument recorded here combines the proof of (b) with the block decomposition.
proofSteps: (a) Choose F′/ℚ_p finite Galois with ρ̄ factoring through H = Gal(F′/ℚ_p); the Hochschild–Serre sequences of SZ.5/drinfeld-tower-ascent (a) compare H¹_ét(M^p_{n,ℂ_p}, k_L)^{Gal_{F′}} with H¹_ét(M^p_{n,F′}, k_L) up to finite-dimensional kernel and cokernel, the latter dual of finite length (SZ.5/finite-length); then Π^geo_n(ρ̄) is built from (ρ̄ ⊗ π)_H as in SZ.6/geometric-multiplicity (CDN proof of Corollary 2.12).

(b) Let π be an irreducible quotient of Π^geo_n(ρ̄); then ρ̄ embeds into Hom^cont_G(π^∨, H¹_ét(M^p_{n,ℂ_p}, k_L)); the ascent of SZ.5/drinfeld-tower-ascent, the comparison sequence of SZ.2/comparison-map and the fact that ρ̄ (irreducible of dimension > 1) does not occur in H⁰_ét(M_∞, k_L) (characters only) give Hom_{Gal}(ρ̄, S¹(π)) ≠ 0. π is not a character since S¹ kills characters (SZ.1/scholze-galois-and-degree-zero (e)); enlarge L so that π is absolutely irreducible, let B be its block and r̄ = ρ̄_B, globalise and form M (SZ.4/residual-globalisation, SZ.4/global-block-occurrence).

If π is supersingular, B = {π} and 0 → π → M → π′ → 0 with π′ a successive extension of copies of π; S⁰(π′) = 0, so S¹(π) ↪ S¹(M) ≅ Ĥ¹_{ψ,λ}(U^𝔭, k_L)_𝔪[𝔪_A] ⊂ r̄ ⊗ N′ (SZ.4/hecke-torsion-comparison, whose isomorphism case applies as r̄ is irreducible, and R31.4 isotypy for Ĥ¹); hence S¹(π) is r̄-isotypic (Scholze Proposition 5.4), so Hom_{Gal}(ρ̄, S¹(π)) ≠ 0 forces ρ̄ ≅ r̄, impossible for d > 2.

If π is not supersingular, r̄ = χ₁ ⊕ χ₂. Lemma 4.24 (d): the kernel of S¹(Z) → S¹(M) is a quotient of S⁰((M/Z)^{SL₂(ℚ_p)}), a successive extension of characters (SZ.1/scholze-galois-and-degree-zero (b)), and the image lies in r̄ ⊗ U, hence has a filtration with graded pieces χ₁ ⊗ U₁ and χ₂ ⊗ U₂; take H-invariants and H¹(H, −). Choose H pro-p, write 0 → X → Y → π → 0 with X, Y ⊂ M; S⁰(π) = 0 gives 0 → (S¹(Y)/S¹(X))^H → S¹(π)^H → S²(X)^H; the first term is controlled by (d) and the last is a successive extension of characters by SZ.3/ludwig-vanishing (d); so Hom_{Gal}(ρ̄, S¹(π)^H) = 0 for absolutely irreducible ρ̄ of dimension ≥ 2, a contradiction.

(c) For d = 2 the same argument excludes every non-supersingular irreducible quotient and forces every supersingular one to be the member Π(ρ̄) of the block of ρ̄; a finite-length object decomposes along blocks (R30.5/blocks), and each block component has an irreducible quotient in its block, so Π^geo_n(ρ̄) lies in the block {Π(ρ̄)}.
acceptance: For every absolutely irreducible three-dimensional ρ̄ (for instance induced from a suitable character of the unramified cubic extension), Π^geo_n(ρ̄) = 0.
For d = 2 and ρ̄ absolutely irreducible, every irreducible constituent of Π^geo_n(ρ̄) is the supersingular Π(ρ̄).
For d = 1, (a) applies and Π^geo_n(χ) has finite length.

nodes.title: Smooth vectors on the Lubin–Tate side (CDN Theorem 4.26)
nodes.statement: Let F = ℚ_p with p > 2, n ≥ 0, LT_{n,ℂ_p} = M_{LT,G_n} ⊗ ℂ_p the level-n Lubin–Tate space (G₀ = GL₂(ℤ_p), G_n = 1 + p^n M₂(ℤ_p) for n ≥ 1), LT^p_{n,ℂ_p} its quotient by p^ℤ ⊂ Z(Ǧ), which descends to ℚ_p, and LT^p_{n,K} its base change to a finite K/ℚ_p; M^p_∞ = M_∞/p^ℤ. Then: (a) the Ǧ-smooth vectors of H¹_ét(LT^p_{n,K}, k_L) form a finite-dimensional k_L-vector space; (b) (Lemma 4.27) for every j, the G-smooth vectors of H¹_ét(M^p_∞, k_L)^{Gal_K × Ǧ_j} form a finite-dimensional space; (c) (Lemma 4.28) H¹_ét(M^p_∞, k_L) contains no non-zero finite-dimensional G-submodule; (d) (Remark 4.29) statement (a) is equivalent to SZ.5/finite-length (a) through the criterion of finite length by smooth vectors of the dual.
hypotheses: F = ℚ_p and p > 2 (through SZ.5/finite-length and SZ.2/moore-sl2-vanishing); the source expects (a) for F ≠ ℚ_p as well, which is not asserted.
proofSteps: (a) As in step 1 of SZ.5/drinfeld-tower-ascent reduce to the smooth vectors of H¹_ét(LT^p_{n,ℂ_p}, k_L)^{Gal_K}; the G_n-torsor M^p_∞ → LT^p_{n,ℂ_p} gives 0 → A → H¹_ét(LT^p_{n,ℂ_p}, k_L) → H¹_ét(M^p_∞, k_L)^{G_n} with A finite-dimensional, so it suffices that colim_j H¹_ét(M^p_∞, k_L)^{G_n × Gal_K × Ǧ_j} is finite-dimensional; by (b) and (c) it is zero.

(b) The ascent sequences give a map H¹_ét(M^p_{j,K}, k_L) → H¹_ét(M^p_∞, k_L)^{Gal_K × Ǧ_j} with finite-dimensional kernel and cokernel; the source is the dual of an admissible finite-length G-representation (SZ.5/finite-length), whose dual has finite-dimensional smooth vectors (ModpRepresentations MP.1/smooth-dual-length); finite-dimensional kernel and cokernel preserve finite-dimensionality of smooth vectors.

(c) A non-zero finite-dimensional smooth G-module is trivial on SL₂(ℚ_p) and contains a character after a finite extension of L, so it suffices that Hom^cont_G(δ, H¹_ét(M_∞, k_L)) = 0 for every smooth character δ (pass from M^p_∞ to M_∞ by step 3 of the ascent). The comparison sequence (SZ.2/comparison-map) gives S¹(δ⁻¹) → Hom^cont_G(δ, H¹_ét(M_∞, k_L)) → H²(SL₂(ℚ_p), δ⁻¹); S¹(δ⁻¹) = 0 by twisting S¹(1) = 0 (SZ.1/scholze-galois-and-degree-zero (d)–(e)), and H²(SL₂(ℚ_p), δ⁻¹) = H²(SL₂(ℚ_p), k_L) = 0 by SZ.2/moore-sl2-vanishing.
(d) Theorem 1.24 (MP.1/smooth-dual-length) with the argument above runs in both directions.

Descent of LT^p_n to ℚ_p: the quotient by p^ℤ ⊂ Z(Ǧ) of the Lubin–Tate tower, like the Drinfeld one, carries an effective Weil descent datum (ET.6a/actions-and-weil-descent; CDN p. 48 asserts the descent).
acceptance: For n = 0 the components of LT^p_{0,K} are open discs and the theorem bounds the Ǧ-smooth vectors of their mod p H¹ over K.
H¹_ét(M^p_∞, k_L) contains no non-zero G-invariant vector.
The finite-dimensional space in (a) contains the contribution of the connected components of LT^p_{n,K}.

gaps.detail: Needed statement (CDN23 Théorème 2.1, p. 21 = Théorème 0.5, p. 5): for F/ℚ_p finite, K/F finite, k ≥ 1 and q ≥ 0, the G′-module H^q_ét(M^ϖ_{n,K}, O_L/p^k) is a profinite O_L-module whose Pontryagin dual is a smooth finitely presented representation of G′ = GL₂(F)/ϖ^ℤ.
